definition_zh: 人族成员；人类这一支（与黑猩猩分化后）的物种
definition_en: a member of the tribe Hominini, the human lineage after its split from the chimpanzee line
core_image: 两条岔开的足迹：一条通向树，一条通向地面，后一条上还叠着更小的脚印
scene: 下层位出土的牙齿被送去测量，报告上只写了族名，没有写属名。 The hominin teeth from the lower layer were smaller than anyone had expected.
sceneCN: 这里「人族成员」指人类这一支的一个物种（第 1 个义项：人族成员）；句意为下层位出土的人族牙齿比任何人预想的都小。

pos.zh: 人族成员（可数，复数 hominins）
人族的；人族特征的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 homo（人）+ -ini（族级分类词尾）→ 人族（分类学上的族名）
拉丁 homo + -idae（科级词尾）→ 人科成员（语义偏移：层级更高，范围更宽）
拉丁 homo + -inae（亚科词尾）→ 人亚科的（语义偏移：层在科与族之间）
拉丁 homo + -oidea（总科词尾）→ 人形总科的；类人猿
australo-（拉丁 australis「南方」）+ pithekos（希腊「猿」）+ -ine → 南方古猿类（语义偏移：人族中较早的一支）
humanus（homo 的形容词）→ 人的；人

senses.title: A member of the tribe Hominini
senses.titleCN: 人族成员：与黑猩猩分化后的人类这一支
senses.definition: a member of the tribe Hominini, the lineage that split from the chimpanzee line
senses.definitionCN: 与黑猩猩一支分化之后的人类谱系成员
senses.example: The hominin teeth from the lower layer were smaller than anyone had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 下层位出土的人族牙齿比任何人预想的都小。
senses.why: The ending -ini marks a tribe, one rank below family; because that tribe was drawn to hold humans and their extinct relatives after the split, the word names a branch rather than a body plan.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ini 标记族，比科低一级；这一族被划定来容纳分化之后的人类及其已灭绝亲属，因此这个词命名的是一个分支，而非一套身体方案。

senses.title: A fossil species on that branch
senses.titleCN: 该支上的化石物种：一个具体物种
senses.definition: a particular extinct species assigned to that branch
senses.definitionCN: 被归入这一支的某一已灭绝物种
senses.example: Each hominin in the collection has been dated by the ash above it.
senses.exampleCN: 藏品中每一个人族物种都是靠其上方的火山灰定年的。
senses.why: A branch is abstract; a species is something you can hold. The noun therefore also names the units that fill museum drawers.
senses.whyCN: 分支是抽象的，物种却能拿在手里；因此这个名词也指填满博物馆抽屉的那些单位。

senses.title: A descriptive adjective
senses.titleCN: 描述性形容词：具人族特征的
senses.definition: showing the traits associated with that branch
senses.definitionCN: 具有该支特征的
senses.example: The hominin foot had an arch, which settled the argument about shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这只人族足部有足弓，平息了关于鞋的争论。
senses.why: As with hominid, the noun doubles as an adjective; here the adjective signals traits taken to mark the branch, such as an arched foot or a flat face.
senses.whyCN: 与 hominid 一样，这个名词兼作形容词；此处形容词表示被认为标记该支的特征，如足弓或扁平的脸。

senses.title: The precise alternative to hominid
senses.titleCN: 对比 hominid 的精确用法：强调层级更窄
senses.definition: the taxonomic term preferred when the narrower branch must be distinguished from the wider family
senses.definitionCN: 需要把较窄的分支与较宽的科区分开时所用的术语
senses.example: The authors write hominin precisely to exclude the gorilla from the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 作者写 hominin 正是为了把大猩猩排除在句子之外。
senses.why: Because hominid widened to include the apes, a narrower word was needed for the human branch; hominin supplied it, and the contrast is now a marker of careful writing.
senses.whyCN: 由于 hominid 变宽而包含猿类，就需要一个更窄的词来指人类这一支；hominin 补上这个位置，如今这组对照成了用词谨慎的标志。

senses.title: Popular 'early hominin'
senses.titleCN: 通俗用法：早期人族成员
senses.definition: in popular science, any early member of the human branch
senses.definitionCN: 通俗科学中人类这一支的任何早期成员
senses.example: The article called every early hominin a candidate for our ancestor.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把每一种早期人族成员都称作我们祖先的候选。
senses.why: Popular writing adopted the technical word because it sounds precise and fits a headline; the popular sense is looser than the taxonomic one.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作采用这个术语，因为它听起来精确又适合标题；通俗义比分类学义宽松。

senses.title: A point on the evolutionary timeline
senses.titleCN: 时间线上的一个节点：谱系图上的位置
senses.definition: a named point or segment on the branching diagram of human ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 人类祖先分叉图上的一个命名节点或段落
senses.example: The chart lists five hominins between the first stone tools and the first hearths.
senses.exampleCN: 图表在最早的石器与最早的灶之间列了五种人族成员。
senses.why: Timelines need countable labels for segments; the noun supplies them, and a chart can then be read left to right.
senses.whyCN: 时间线需要可数的段标，这个名词正好提供；图表于是可以从左读到右。

senses.title: A unit of the fossil record
senses.titleCN: 化石记录的单位：可比较的一批标本
senses.definition: a comparative unit of the fossil record, often a named sample
senses.definitionCN: 化石记录中的比较单位，常是一个命名样本
senses.example: The hominin sample from the cave is too small to settle the question.
senses.exampleCN: 这个洞穴的人族样本太小，回答不了这个问题。
senses.why: In practice specimens are grouped into samples before any statistic is run, and the noun is used for those groups as well as for the species.
senses.whyCN: 实际上，任何统计之前都要把标本归成样本，而这个名词也用来指这些组，而不只是物种。

senses.title: Evidence in a taxonomic dispute
senses.titleCN: 分类争议中的证据：用来主张拆分或合并
senses.definition: a category whose boundaries are argued over in debates about splitting and lumping
senses.definitionCN: 在「拆」与「并」之争中被争论边界的类别
senses.example: Whether that jaw is a hominin at all is the whole dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 那块下颌到底算不算人族成员，正是整场争议。
senses.why: Where a rank is drawn is a decision, not a discovery; naming a fossil a hominin is therefore a claim that can be contested, and the word carries that argument inside it.
senses.whyCN: 层级画在哪里是决定，而非发现；把一块化石称作 hominin 因此是一个可被反驳的主张，这个词本身带着这场争论。

intro.en: Hominin is the newest of the family words, formed when twentieth-century taxonomy needed a rank narrower than the family; its stem is the old Latin word for a person.
intro.cn: hominin 是这一族词里最新的一个，形成于 20 世纪分类学需要一个比科更窄的层级之时；其词干仍是古老的拉丁语「人」。

items.en: Homo, hominis meant 'human being'; its deeper origin is disputed, and the humus 'earth' connection is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: homo, hominis 意为「人」；更深来源有争议，与 humus「土地」的联系是假说而非已证实的派生。

items.en: The family name Hominidae was already established in the nineteenth century, built on the same stem with the family ending.
items.cn: 科名 Hominidae 在 19 世纪已确立，用同一词干加科级词尾构成。

items.en: When comparative genetics placed the great apes inside the family, the older word hominid no longer marked the human branch alone.
items.cn: 当比较遗传学把大猿放进这个科，旧的 hominid 便不再单独标记人类这一支。

items.en: Taxonomists drew a tribe inside the subfamily to hold humans and their extinct relatives after the chimpanzee split, and named it Hominini with the tribe ending -ini.
items.cn: 分类学者在人亚科内划出一个族，容纳黑猩猩分化后的人类及其已灭绝亲属，并以族级词尾 -ini 命名为 Hominini。

items.en: English formed hominin from the tribe name in the later twentieth century; it spread quickly because museum labels needed a short precise word.
items.cn: 英语在 20 世纪后期由族名构成 hominin；它传播很快，因为博物馆标签需要一个简短精确的词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use is dated only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of homo remains unknown, so proposed forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见年代只有约数；homo 在拉丁语之前的来源仍不明，所拟形式均为重构。

note.en: Group one holds the rank words that differ only by their endings; group two holds the wider categories a hominin also belongs to.
note.cn: 第一组是仅靠词尾区分的层级词；第二组是人族成员同时所属的更宽类别。

entries.definition: A member of the family Hominidae, which now includes the great apes; correct but less precise for the human branch.
entries.definitionCN: 人科成员，今含大猿；说法正确，但指人类这一支时不够精确。

entries.definition: A member of the subfamily Homininae, the African apes and humans together.
entries.definitionCN: 人亚科成员，即非洲猿与人类。

entries.definition: A member of the superfamily Hominoidea, the widest of these categories.
entries.definitionCN: 人形总科成员，是这些类别中最宽的。

entries.definition: A member of Homo sapiens, the only surviving hominin.
entries.definitionCN: 智人成员，是唯一存续至今的人族成员。

entries.definition: A member of the genus Australopithecus and its allies, early hominins with small brains.
entries.definitionCN: 南方古猿属及其近亲的成员，是脑量小的早期人族。

entries.definition: A member of Homo neanderthalensis, a hominin that interbred with modern humans.
entries.definitionCN: 尼安德特人，曾与现代人杂交的人族成员。

entries.definition: A member of the order Primates, which contains the hominins among many others.
entries.definitionCN: 灵长目成员，人族只是其中一支。

entries.definition: An earlier population from which a later one descends; the word makes no claim about tribe or family.
entries.definitionCN: 后代所出自的较早群体；该词不对族或科作断言。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real rank endings, real fossil names and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的层级词尾、真实化石名与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ini is the tribe ending, so hominin is one rank narrower than hominid and one wider than a species.
normal.cn: -ini 是族级词尾，因此 hominin 比 hominid 窄一级，比物种宽一级。

normal.en: The tribe was drawn to hold the human branch after the chimpanzee split, so the word names a branch, not a shape.
normal.cn: 这个族是为容纳黑猩猩分化后的人类一支而划的，因此这个词命名分支，而非形状。

normal.en: The family runs Hominini, hominin, hominid, hominine, hominoid, australopithecine.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 Hominini、hominin、hominid、hominine、hominoid、australopithecine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: early hominin, hominin fossils, the hominin lineage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：早期人族成员、人族化石、人族谱系。

normal.en: In a sentence about ancestry, hominin keeps the gorilla out; hominid lets it in.
normal.cn: 在谈祖先的句子里，hominin 把大猩猩挡在外面，hominid 则放它进来。

abstract.en: Picture two footprints diverging, one toward trees and one toward open ground.
abstract.cn: 想象两串脚印分开，一串通向树，一串通向开阔地。

abstract.en: Picture a label so precise that it excludes a cousin standing beside the case.
abstract.cn: 想象一张精确到把展柜旁的堂亲排除在外的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a chart whose left edge changes every time a new jaw is found.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图表，每找到一块新下颌，左端就要改一次。

examples.en: The hominin lineage lost a robust jaw before it gained a large brain.
examples.cn: 人族谱系先失去粗壮的下颌，之后才得到大容量的脑。

examples.en: Museum labels were rewritten from hominid to hominin after the taxonomy changed.
examples.cn: 分类改变之后，博物馆标签从 hominid 改写为 hominin。

examples.en: A single hominin tooth can support two incompatible reconstructions.
examples.cn: 一颗人族牙齿可以同时支持两套互不相容的重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: homin（人）+ in（族级词尾）＝ 人族成员；记「比科窄一级，比种宽一级」。

root: 新拉丁 Hominini：拉丁 homo（homin-「人」）+ -ini（族级分类词尾）；homo 更深来源不确定，与 humus「土地」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses narrow one word from a tribe to a tooth: the branch member, a fossil species, an adjective, the precise alternative to hominid, the popular ancestor, a point on a chart, a sample in the record, and a claim in a taxonomic dispute.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个词从族缩到一颗牙：分支成员、化石物种、形容词、hominid 的精确替代、通俗祖先、图表节点、记录中的样本，以及分类争议中的主张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sets of footprints splitting, with smaller prints laid over the one that leads to open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：两串分开的脚印，通向开阔地的那一串上叠着更小的脚印。

branches.en: BRANCH AND UNIT: the tribe as a whole, then the countable species that fills it.
branches.cn: 分支与单位：先是整个族，再是填满它的可数物种。

branches.en: SHAPE AND PRECISION: an adjective for traits, and a term chosen to keep the apes out.
branches.cn: 形状与精确：指特征的形容词，以及为把猿挡在外面而选的术语。

branches.en: STORY AND CHART: the headline ancestor, and the labelled point on a timeline.
branches.cn: 故事与图表：标题里的祖先，与时间线上带标签的一点。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE: specimens grouped before any number is calculated.
branches.cn: 样本：任何计算之前先归好的标本组。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: where a rank is drawn is a decision that can be contested.
branches.cn: 争论：层级画在哪里是一个可被反驳的决定。

intro.en: Hominin is the same Latin stem as hominid with a different rank ending, and the endings are what separate the four commonly confused words.
intro.cn: hominin 与 hominid 共用同一拉丁词干，只是层级词尾不同，而词尾正是区分四个易混词的关键。

latinIntro.en: Latin homo supplies homin-; New Latin endings mark the ranks, -idae family, -inae subfamily, -ini tribe and -oidea superfamily, and English adds -in for a member of the tribe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 homo 提供 homin-；新拉丁词尾标记层级：-idae 科、-inae 亚科、-ini 族、-oidea 总科，英语再加 -in 指该族成员。

items.example: The stem is shared with every rank name in this family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干与本族各层级名称共用。

items.example: The ending is the only thing that separates hominin from hominid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾是 hominin 与 hominid 的唯一区别。

items.example: The word names the narrowest rank in common use.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指日常使用中最窄的层级。

items.example: The wider word now admits the great apes.
items.exampleCN: 较宽的这个词如今容纳大猿。

items.example: The intermediate word names the African apes and humans together.
items.exampleCN: 中间这个词指非洲猿与人类的合集。

items.example: The widest word takes in all the apes.
items.exampleCN: 最宽的这个词包含所有猿类。

items.example: The tribe name is capitalized and italicized.
The compound names an early part of the tribe.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名族中较早的一支。

items.structure: Neanderthal, a German valley, + -ensis in the scientific name
items.example: The place name became a species name and then a common noun.
items.exampleCN: 地名先成为种名，再成为普通名词。

latinEntries.structure: Hominini (New Latin, f. plural, tribe rank)
latinEntries.meaning: the tribe of humans and their extinct relatives
latinEntries.meaningCN: 人类及其已灭绝亲属的族

definition_zh: n. 暗杀；行刺（尤指政治人物）；（名誉的）毁谤
definition_en: The murder of a prominent person, usually for political reasons; figuratively, the deliberate destruction of a reputation.
core_image: 一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了
scene: 广播里传来总统遇刺的消息。 The radio reported the assassination of the president.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assassination 指出于政治等目的杀害重要人物。

pos.zh: 暗杀；行刺；名誉毁谤

senses.title: The killing of a prominent person
senses.definition: the deliberate murder of a public figure, usually to change or punish a political order
senses.definitionCN: 有意杀害公众人物，通常为了改变或惩罚某种政治秩序
senses.example: The assassination plunged the country into mourning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次暗杀使全国陷入哀悼。
senses.why: What separates this word from murder is the target: the victim matters to many people, so the act is public.
senses.whyCN: 把这个词与 murder 区分开的是目标：受害者对许多人都有分量，所以这一行为是公共性的。

senses.title: The killing of a reputation
senses.definition: a sustained attempt to destroy someone standing, as in the phrase character assassination
senses.definitionCN: 持续地摧毁某人的声望，如「人格毁谤」这一说法
senses.example: The campaign was character assassination, not debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那场攻势是人格毁谤，不是辩论。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essentials: a chosen target, a planned strike and something that cannot be brought back.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了核心要素：选定的目标、有计划的打击，以及无法挽回的东西。

intro.en: Assassination comes from assassin, traced by the traditional account to Arabic hashshashin, a name applied to a secretive order in Persia and Syria.
intro.cn: assassination 出自 assassin；按传统说法，后者源自阿拉伯语 hashshashin，是对波斯与叙利亚一个秘密教团的称呼。

items.en: The traditional account links the word to a name for a secretive order whose members carried out targeted killings.
items.cn: 传统说法把这个词与一个秘密教团的称号相联，其成员执行有目标的杀害。

items.en: Crusaders brought back stories and the name, and the tale of drug use is now doubted by historians.
items.cn: 十字军带回故事与这个称号，而其中「用药」的说法如今已被史家质疑。

items.en: Medieval Latin assassinus named a hired killer, stripping the word of its sect and keeping the act.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 指受雇的杀手，剥去教团背景，只留下行为本身。

items.en: Italian assassinare turned the noun into a verb meaning to murder a prominent person.
items.cn: 意大利语 assassinare 把名词变成动词，意为杀害重要人物。

items.en: English records the noun from the mid seventeenth century, soon standard in political reporting.
items.cn: 英语从十七世纪中叶起记录这个名词，很快成为政治报道的标准用词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century journalism fixed character assassination for the planned ruin of a name.
items.cn: 十九世纪新闻业固定了 character assassination 一语，指有计划地毁掉一个人的名声。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the assassin family and adds a word that only sounds similar; the near-meaning group grades killings by scale and framing.
note.cn: 形近组保留 assassin 词族，并加上一个只是听着像的词；近义组按规模与说法区分各种杀害。

entries.definition: To murder a prominent person.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害重要人物。

entries.definition: A person who kills for hire or a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为报酬或信念杀人的刺客。

entries.definition: The killing of many people at once.
entries.definitionCN: 一次杀害许多人。

entries.definition: The state of being intensely interested.
entries.definitionCN: 被强烈吸引的状态。

entries.definition: The unlawful killing of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 非法杀害一个人。

entries.definition: Killing carried out as a penalty.
entries.definitionCN: 作为刑罚实施的处死。

entries.definition: A killing, a word favoured in reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，报道中偏用的词。

entries.definition: Killing described as mere removal.
entries.definitionCN: 把杀害说成「清除」。

normalIntro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation: the act named after the doer, and the doer named after an old order.
normalIntro.cn: assassination 就是 assassin 加 -ation：以行为者命名的行为，而行为者又以一个古老教团命名。

normal.en: Assassin, assassinate, assassination form one chain.
normal.cn: assassin、assassinate、assassination 是一条链。

normal.en: The target must be a public figure.
normal.cn: 目标必须是公众人物。

normal.en: An assassination attempt is a failed one.
normal.cn: an assassination attempt 指未成功的行刺。

normal.en: Character assassination attacks a name, not a body.
normal.cn: character assassination 攻击名声，不是身体。

normal.en: Murder is the wider word, this one is specific.
normal.cn: murder 更宽泛，本词更具体。

abstract.en: Picture one shot and one empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一声枪响与一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole street lowering its flags.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街降下半旗。

abstract.en: Think of a name torn down line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被一行行撕掉。

examples.en: The plot ended in assassination.
examples.cn: 那场阴谋以暗杀收场。

examples.en: Two assassinations shook the region that year.
examples.cn: 那一年两起暗杀震动了该地区。

examples.en: He called the article character assassination.
examples.cn: 他称那篇文章是人格毁谤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：assassin「刺客」+ -ation「行为」——刺客干的那件事，就是暗杀 assassination。

root: 阿拉伯语 hashshashin 经十字军传闻与中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 变成「受雇杀手」，意大利语 assassinare 转为动词，英语加 -ation 于十七世纪中叶构成 assassination。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses destroy something public and irreplaceable: a person who held a position, and a name that took years to build.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都摧毁某种公共而不可替代之物：占据某个位置的人，以及多年才建立起来的名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shot, and a public place suddenly empty
core.cn: 核心意象：一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了

branches.en: A radio bulletin and lowered flags.
branches.cn: 一则广播与降下的旗。

branches.en: A plot that ends in one shot.
branches.cn: 以一声枪响收场的阴谋。

branches.en: A name torn down line by line.
branches.cn: 被一行行撕掉的名声。

branches.en: A campaign that is not debate.
branches.cn: 并非辩论的攻势。

branches.en: A chosen public target, struck by plan.
branches.cn: 按计划打击选定的公共目标。

intro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation through the verb -ate; the surrounding political vocabulary is built from -al, -ist and -ism.
intro.cn: assassination 是 assassin 经动词后缀 -ate 再加 -ation 构成；周边的政治词汇由 -al、-ist 与 -ism 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The word is Arabic at heart, but Medieval Latin assassinus and assassinare carried it into Europe; Latin caedes, slaughter, names the act beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词内核来自阿拉伯语，但中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 与 assassinare 把它带进欧洲；旁边的拉丁语 caedes「杀戮」指同一行为。

definition_zh: 坚持；面对困难仍不放弃；在漫长过程中持续投入；坚守立场或信仰
definition_en: to keep doing something in a steady way even when it is hard, slow or discouraging
core_image: 一条长长的上坡石阶，雨越下越大，走路的人一步接一步往上，始终没有停下
scene: 哪怕实验记录被退回了三次，她仍然每天清晨回到同一张桌子前，把流程再走一遍。 She perseveres with the experiment long after her first plan failed.
sceneCN: 这里 persevere 指「面对阻力仍持续做同一件事」（第 1 个义项：顶着挫败继续行动）；句意为最早的方案失败很久之后，她仍坚持做这项实验。图中可辨识物件：湿透的石阶、被雨打湿的记录纸、一直向前的脚印。

pos.zh: 坚持；不屈不挠地继续（与 in、with、at 等介词搭配）

collocations.phrase: persevere in the face of failure

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示状态的名词后缀构成，语义由「持续做下去」转为「持续做下去的状态与品质」
由动词加表示性质的形容词后缀构成，语义由「坚持下去」转为「具有坚持特征的」
在形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「有毅力的」转为「以有毅力的方式」
借拉丁语现在分词形式进入英语的形容词，语义与「坚持不懈的」相同，现代用法较少

senses.title: Keep acting despite resistance
senses.definition: to go on doing something although it is difficult, and to refuse to stop because of setbacks
senses.definitionCN: 尽管事情困难，仍继续做下去，不因挫折而停下
senses.example: She perseveres with the experiment long after her first plan failed.
senses.exampleCN: 最早的方案失败很久之后，她仍坚持做这项实验。
senses.why: per- intensifies and severus means strict or serious, so persevere originally meant to hold to something strictly, without letting go.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表「彻底」，词根意为「严格、严肃」，因此该词本义是「严格地守住一件事，不松手」。

senses.title: Continue a course once begun
senses.definition: to carry a course of action through to its end rather than abandoning it halfway
senses.definitionCN: 把已经开始的做法一路做完，而不是中途放弃
senses.example: He persevered in his daily readings even during the busiest term.
senses.exampleCN: 即便在最忙的一个学期里，他也坚持每天朗读。
senses.why: the idea of holding fast to a strict rule explains why the word suits steady habits, not only dramatic struggles.
senses.whyCN: 「严格守住一条规矩」这层意思，解释了为什么该词既用于惊天动地的抗争，也用于日复一日的习惯。

senses.title: Hold to a purpose under pressure
senses.titleCN: 顶着压力守住既定目标
senses.definition: to remain committed to a decided aim when others argue against it or when it becomes unpopular
senses.definitionCN: 当他人反对或这件事不再受欢迎时，仍忠于已定的目标
senses.example: The team persevered with the proposal despite loud criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管批评声很大，团队仍坚持这份提案。
senses.why: a strict, serious holding of a purpose is the mental version of the uphill road: the aim stays fixed while conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 「严肃地守住目标」是那条上坡路在心理层面的版本：条件在变，目标不变。

senses.title: Stay with a long inquiry
senses.titleCN: 在长周期研究里持续投入
senses.definition: to keep working on a long piece of research or creative work across years of slow progress
senses.definitionCN: 在进展缓慢的多年研究中或长期创作中持续投入
senses.example: The astronomers persevered for a decade before the signal made sense.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家坚持了十年，那个信号才变得可解。
senses.why: the word measures duration as much as difficulty, so it fits inquiries that pay off only after many seasons.
senses.whyCN: 该词既量难度，也量时间，因此特别适合那些要过很多季才有回报的探究。

senses.title: Endure hardship without quitting
senses.titleCN: 在困境中默默撑住而不退出
senses.definition: to bear continuing discomfort or misfortune rather than walk away from the situation
senses.definitionCN: 承受持续的不适或不幸，而不是从处境中抽身离开
senses.example: The settlers persevered through a winter without fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 拓荒者熬过了一个没有燃料的冬天。
senses.why: endurance shades into perseverance when the hardship is not a single event but a stretch of time that must be lived through.
senses.whyCN: 当艰难不是一次事件，而是一段必须活过去的时间，忍耐就变成了坚持。

senses.title: Remain in a state or opinion
senses.definition: to continue in a particular condition or opinion, especially when others have moved on
senses.definitionCN: 继续停留在某种状态或看法里，尤其是在别人已经改变之后
senses.example: He persevered in his doubts long after the evidence had settled the question.
senses.exampleCN: 证据早已把问题定了下来，他却长时间固守着自己的疑虑。
senses.why: the older construction with in marks the state one stays inside, which is the same root idea as staying on the road.
senses.whyCN: 旧说法在动词后接一个表示「在……之中」的介词，标出人「待在」某种状态里，这与「继续走在路上」是同一个词根意象。

senses.title: Insist on a point in argument
senses.definition: to keep repeating or defending a position in a discussion instead of conceding it
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中反复重申或捍卫某个立场，而不肯让步
senses.example: She persevered in her objection until the chair allowed a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚持她的反对意见，直到主席同意表决。
senses.why: holding strictly to a statement is the verbal face of the same stubborn steadiness that the road image shows.
senses.whyCN: 严格守住一句话，与那条路上表现出的倔强稳定是同一件事的口头版本。

senses.title: Stay faithful to a belief
senses.definition: to remain loyal to a faith or a set of beliefs to the end of one's life
senses.definitionCN: 对某种信仰或一套信念忠诚到底，直至生命终点
senses.example: Many believers persevered in their faith under persecution.
senses.exampleCN: 许多信徒在迫害之下仍坚守信仰。
senses.why: religious writers borrowed the Latin verb for holding to the faith, and that use kept the sense of holding fast at its purest.
senses.whyCN: 宗教写作者借用了这个拉丁动词表示「守住信仰」，这一用法把「紧抓不放」的意思保存得最纯粹。

intro.en: Persevere comes from Latin perseverare 'to persist, to abide by strictly', built on per- 'thoroughly' and severus 'strict, grave'. The deeper origin of severus is not established, and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁语 perseverare「坚持、严格遵守」，由 per-「彻底」与 severus「严格、严肃」构成。severus 更深的来源尚未查明，年代均为约数。

items.en: Severus meant 'strict, serious, grave'. Its deeper source is not settled; the suggestions that link it to a root for 'heavy' or to a word for 'setting apart' are hypotheses, not demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: severus 意为「严格、严肃、庄重」。其更深来源无定论；把它与表示「沉重」的词根或表示「分开」的词相联系的看法都只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus severus produced perseverare 'to abide by strictly, to persist', a verb of holding to a rule without slackening.
items.cn: per-「彻底」加 severus 构成 perseverare「严格遵守、坚持」，是一个表示「毫不放松地守住规矩」的动词。

items.en: The abstract noun perseverantia 'steadfastness' appears in late Latin prose, and it is the direct model for the English noun.
items.cn: 抽象名词 perseverantia「坚定不移」出现在晚期拉丁语散文中，是英语中对应名词的直接原型。

items.en: Old French perseverer carried the verb into Middle English in the fourteenth century, at first in religious and moral writing.
items.cn: 古法语 perseverer 在十四世纪把这个动词带入中古英语，最早见于宗教与道德论述。

items.en: English divinity fixed the phrase to persevere in the faith, meaning to hold out to the end rather than to start well.
items.cn: 英语神学固定了「在信仰中坚持到底」的说法，强调不是开头好，而是守到最后。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of severus): no exact first citation is recorded for the everyday sense of keeping at a task, and any Indo-European form offered for severus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（severus 的更深词源）：日常「坚持做一件事」的义项没有确切的最早书证；凡为 severus 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one collects look-alikes built with per- or with a similar shape but a different root; group two collects verbs of continuing that differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是形近但词根不同的词；第二组是都表示「继续」、但侧重不同的动词。

entries.definition: Per- 'thoroughly' plus suadere 'to advise': to talk someone into a view, with no element of endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per-「彻底」加 suadere「劝告」构成：以言辞使人接受某种看法，与「熬住」无关。

entries.definition: From Latin pro- 'forward' plus sequi 'to follow': to chase or follow something, not to outlast it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」：追赶或追随某物，而不是熬过它。

entries.definition: Prae- 'before' plus servare 'to keep': to keep something safe from harm, which is about protection, not persistence.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prae-「在前」加 servare「保存」构成：使某物免受损害，说的是保护而非持续。

entries.definition: Per- 'thoroughly' plus vertere 'to turn': turned the wrong way, deliberately contrary, with no link to strictness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per-「彻底」加 vertere「转」构成：方向转反了、故意与人相反，与「严格」无关。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the Latin verb: strict, harsh, not allowing slack, so it is the closest relative in form and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 就是那个拉丁动词背后的形容词：严格、严厉、不许松懈，是形与义都最近的同族词。

entries.definition: To continue in an action or state, often with the note of lasting longer than expected; it can describe things as well as people.
entries.definitionCN: 继续做某事或保持某状态，常带「比预想更久」的意味；人与物都可用。

entries.definition: To suffer something difficult patiently; the focus is on the weight borne, while perseverance adds the choice to keep going.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心承受艰难，重点在承担的分量；而该词另加了一层「主动选择继续」。

entries.definition: To state or demand something firmly and refuse to drop it, usually in speech rather than in long effort.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地声明或要求某事而不肯作罢，多用于言语，而非长期行动。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for continuing an activity; it reports the fact without praising the grit.
entries.definitionCN: 继续某项活动的日常说法；只陈述事实，不含赞许毅力的意味。

entries.definition: An informal phrase for not abandoning a task; close to the meaning but limited to relaxed speech.
entries.definitionCN: 不放弃某项任务的口语说法；意思相近，但只用于轻松的口语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Per- 'thoroughly' plus severus 'strict': to be strict with yourself all the way through.
normal.cn: 前缀表「彻底」，词根表「严格」：对自己一路严格到底。

normal.en: The family runs persevere, perseverance, persevering, perseveringly, perseverant.
normal.cn: 同族词包括动词、名词、形容词、副词与少用的拉丁式形容词五种形态。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the struggle: persevere with a task, persevere in the face of failure, persevere to the end.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这份挣扎：坚持任务、在失败面前不退、坚持到底。

normal.en: The shared root shows in severe and severity, where the same strictness appears without the effort of continuing.
normal.cn: 同根词 severe 与 severity 里能看到同一份「严厉」，只是不带「持续」的意味。

normal.en: The noun perseverance is the one used in praise: perseverance wins long races.
normal.cn: 名词形式常用于称赞：毅力能赢下长跑。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that keeps burning although the window will not stay shut.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛，窗子关不严，它却一直燃着。

abstract.en: Picture a river that keeps cutting the same channel through new rock each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，每年都在新岩层里把同一条河道切下去。

abstract.en: Picture a hand writing the same sentence again and again until the ink runs out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把同一句话一遍遍写下去，直到墨水用尽。

examples.en: The researchers persevered through four failed seasons before the method worked.
examples.cn: 研究人员熬过四个失败的季节，方法才奏效。

examples.en: You will not master the cello unless you persevere with the scales.
examples.cn: 如果不在音阶上坚持，你就学不好大提琴。

examples.en: She persevered in her request until the committee finally replied.
examples.cn: 她一直坚持提出请求，委员会最终给了答复。

dict_mnemonic.text: per（彻底）+ severe（严厉）——对自己一路严厉下去，就是坚持

root: 拉丁 perseverare「坚持、严格遵守」= per-（彻底）+ severus「严格、严肃」；severus 更深来源不确定，相关词根联系均为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a person stays on the same road while the weather, the critics and the years change around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：路不变，人在上面不走开，而天气、旁人与岁月都在变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker on a long uphill stair in heavy rain, one step after another, never turning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：大雨里有人走在长长的上坡石阶上，一步接一步，从不回头。

branches.en: THE ROAD ITSELF: start moving and keep the same motion to the end.
branches.cn: 路本身：起步行进，并把同一个动作做到终点。

branches.en: HOLDING A POSITION: a purpose or an argument is gripped as tightly as a handrail.
branches.cn: 守住位置：目标或论点像扶手一样被紧紧握住。

branches.en: LONG TIME: years of slow work are the road stretched out.
branches.cn: 长时间：多年缓慢的工作，就是把路拉得很长。

branches.en: BEARING WEATHER: the rain is endured rather than escaped.
branches.cn: 承受天气：雨是被熬过去的，而不是躲开的。

branches.en: STAYING INSIDE: remaining in a state or a faith is standing still on the road rather than leaving it.
branches.cn: 待在原处：留在某种状态或信仰里，就是站在原地而不离开这条路。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb held together by an intensive prefix and a root adjective, and both parts also build other English words, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词，由一个表加强的前缀和一个形容词性词根合成，两部分都还构成别的英语词，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin severus yields severe, severity and asseverate; per- yields perceive, persist and pervade, though each of those has its own root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 severus 衍生出 severe、severity 与 asseverate；per- 还见于 perceive、persist 与 pervade，但它们各自另有词根。

items.example: The prefix pushes the action to its limit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作推到极限。

items.example: The root supplies the note of strictness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了「严格」的意味。
他们坚持把这件重建做完。

items.example: A persevering reader finished the whole archive.
items.exampleCN: 一位有毅力的读者读完了整座档案。

items.example: She wrote perseveringly for six hours.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持不懈地写了六个小时。

items.example: The severity of the rule left no room to bend.
items.exampleCN: 这条规矩的严厉程度不留任何通融余地。

items.example: A severe winter closed the pass.
items.exampleCN: 一个严酷的冬天封住了山口。

items.example: He asseverated that the record was complete.
items.exampleCN: 他郑重声明记录是完整的。

latinEntries.structure: severus, severa, severum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: vt. 把…装入箱中；包住；围住；把…封在壳里
definition_en: to enclose something completely in a case or covering
core_image: 修复师把碎陶片放进定制的泡沫凹槽，合上盖子，整件器物被一层软壳严严包住
scene: 博物馆要把碎陶片封进定制的泡沫凹槽里，再合上盖子。 The museum will encase the fragments in fitted foam.
sceneCN: 这里 encase 指「把…封在壳里」（第 1 个义项：用外壳或覆盖物完全包住）；句意是博物馆要把这些碎片封进定制的泡沫里。

pos.zh: 把…装入箱中；包住；封在壳里

senses.title: To enclose in a case
senses.definition: to enclose something completely in a case or covering
senses.definitionCN: （动词）用箱子或覆盖物把某物完全包住
senses.example: The museum will encase the fragments in fitted foam.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆要把这些碎片封进定制的泡沫里。
senses.why: A lid closing over pottery shards lying in cut-out foam
senses.whyCN: 盖子合上，罩住躺在泡沫凹槽里的陶片

senses.title: To surround tightly
senses.definition: to surround something closely on all sides
senses.definitionCN: （动词）从四面紧紧围住某物
senses.example: Ice encased the hull of the ship for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 冰把船体紧紧包住了三个星期。
senses.why: A hull held in a white shell that has to be chipped away
senses.whyCN: 船体被一层白壳裹住，得一点点凿开

senses.title: To protect by covering
senses.definition: to cover something so that it is protected from damage
senses.definitionCN: （动词）覆盖某物使其免受损坏
senses.example: Workers encased the old pipes in a sleeve of concrete.
senses.exampleCN: 工人给旧管道套上一层混凝土外壳。
senses.why: A soft sleeve drawn over a pipe before the trench is filled
senses.whyCN: 填沟之前，一层软套被拉过管道

intro.en: Encase is en- plus case, from Latin capsa, a box; to encase is to put a thing into a box, and then to make the box itself the covering.
intro.cn: encase 由 en- 加 case 组成，case 来自拉丁语 capsa（盒子）；encase 就是把东西放进盒子，进而让盒子本身成为覆盖物。

items.en: Capsa means a box or case for holding things.
items.cn: capsa 意为装东西的盒子、箱子。

items.en: Old French casse carries the box sense into English case.
items.cn: 古法语 casse 把盒子的意思带进英语 case。

items.en: English forms encase from en- plus case, meaning to put in a case.
items.cn: 英语由 en- 加 case 造出 encase，意为装入箱中。

items.en: Travel writing uses encase of ships and limbs held in ice.
items.cn: 游记用 encase 指被冰裹住的船与肢体。

items.en: The noun encasement appears for a protective outer layer.
items.cn: 名词 encasement 出现，指保护性的外层。

items.en: Engineering uses encase for pipes and cables given a sleeve.
items.cn: 工程用 encase 指给管道与电缆加套。

note.en: Encase, case and casing share Latin capsa, a box; enclose and encapsulate are the nearest verbs, but enclose stresses a boundary and encapsulate a small shell.

dict_mnemonic.text: encase ＝ en-（使进入）＋ case（箱子，拉丁 capsa）＝「放进箱子里」→ 包住、封住。名词 case 箱子、情况，名词 casing 外壳、套管，名词 encasement 包住、外壳。三类用法：封壳 encase in glass 封在玻璃里、encase in plastic 用塑料封装；紧裹 be encased in ice 被冰封住、encase the body 包住躯体；保护 encase in concrete 用混凝土包住、encase completely 完全包住。常见被动：the pipes were encased 管道被套住。注意 encase 强调四面贴紧地包住，enclose 强调围出一个边界，encapsulate 强调装进一个小壳或概括成一句话。case 还有情况一义，与箱子义同形。

root: en-（使进入）＋ case（箱子，拉丁 capsa）→ encase（放入箱中 → 包住；封住）

senses.title: To deprive of a loved one
senses.definition: to leave someone suddenly without a relative or friend, especially by death

senses.title: To strip away something valued

senses.why: The violent snatching widens from persons to what persons give.

definition_zh: 濒危物种；有灭绝危险的物种
definition_en: a species whose numbers have fallen so low that it is in danger of dying out
core_image: 一份名录上排着一行行名字，每一行旁边都空出一个位置，像候诊室里一个个空椅子
scene: 这里指「濒危物种」。 Every endangered species on the list receives a recovery plan.
sceneCN: 这里 endangered species 指「被认定有灭绝危险、因而需要干预的物种」（第 2 个义项：依法列名并附带恢复义务的物种）；句意为名录上的每个濒危物种都配有一份恢复计划。图中可辨识物件：名录纸页、逐行名字、空出的位置、恢复计划表格。

pos.zh: 濒危物种（可数；单复数同形，species 本身单复数同形）

senses.title: A species at risk of dying out
senses.definition: a species whose remaining numbers are too low to be safe in the long run
senses.definitionCN: 剩余数量过低、长期难以存续的物种
senses.example: Every endangered species on the list receives a recovery plan.
senses.exampleCN: 名录上的每个濒危物种都配有一份恢复计划。
senses.why: the phrase simply joins the adjective of risk to the noun for a kind of living thing, and the risk is the whole point.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只是把表示风险的形容词接到表示生物种类的名词上，而风险正是它的全部要点。

senses.title: A species listed by statute
senses.definition: a species formally placed on a legal list, which brings protection and recovery duties
senses.definitionCN: 被正式列入法律名录的物种，随之附带保护与恢复义务
senses.example: The snail became an endangered species under federal law.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蜗牛依据联邦法律成为濒危物种。
senses.why: law needs a countable, listable unit, and this phrase supplies one, turning a condition into a status.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个可数、可列名的单位，这个短语正好提供，把一种状况变成一种身份。

senses.title: One rung of a ranking
senses.definition: the category between vulnerable and critically endangered in conservation rankings
senses.definitionCN: 保护等级排序中介于易危与极危的一档
senses.example: The cat is officially an endangered species, not yet critically so.
senses.exampleCN: 这种猫正式列为濒危物种，尚未到极危。
senses.why: a ranked scale needs names for each step, and this phrase became the step that sits one above vulnerable.
senses.whyCN: 分级尺度需要为每一档命名，这个短语就成了高于易危的那一档。

senses.title: A species in rapid decline
senses.definition: a species whose population is falling fast even if it is still numerous
senses.definitionCN: 指数量虽仍多但下滑迅速的物种
senses.example: The shark is an endangered species despite large catches still being reported.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管仍报告大量渔获，这种鲨鱼已是濒危物种。
senses.why: what matters is the direction of the curve, not the current height, so a still-numerous species can carry the label.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于曲线的方向而非当下的高度，因此数量仍多的物种也能带这个标签。

senses.title: A flagship on a campaign poster
senses.titleCN: 作为宣传旗舰的濒危物种
senses.definition: a species used in campaigns because its plight attracts attention and money
senses.definitionCN: 因处境引人注意、能带来关注与资金的宣传用物种
senses.example: The panda became the endangered species on every poster.
senses.exampleCN: 熊猫成了每张海报上的濒危物种。
senses.why: campaigns need a face rather than a list, so one species stands in for the category.
senses.whyCN: 宣传活动需要一张脸而非一份清单，因此由某个物种代表整个类别。

senses.title: Protection as policy and budget
senses.titleCN: 作为政策与预算的保护对象
senses.definition: the object of laws, budgets and recovery programmes rather than a single animal
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、预算与恢复计划的对象，而非单个动物
senses.example: Spending on endangered species has risen every year since the act passed.
senses.exampleCN: 自该法通过以来，濒危物种相关支出逐年上升。
senses.why: a category that can be funded becomes a budget line, and the phrase shifts from animals to programmes.
senses.whyCN: 可拨款的类别会变成预算条目，短语便从动物转向计划。

senses.title: A vanishing kind of anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：正在消失的一类人或物
senses.definition: a group or type of thing that is becoming rare and may disappear, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指日益稀少、可能消失的一类人或事物
senses.example: The corner bookshop is an endangered species in this city.
senses.exampleCN: 街角书店在这座城市里已是濒危物种。
senses.why: once the phrase is familiar, it can be borrowed for any type that is being pushed out of existence.
senses.whyCN: 短语一旦为人熟悉，就可借用于任何正被挤出存在的类型。

senses.title: The term inside a statute
senses.titleCN: 法律条文内的固定用语
senses.definition: the exact wording used by statutes and treaties to define what counts as protected
senses.definitionCN: 法规与条约用来界定受保护对象的固定措辞
senses.example: The definition of endangered species in the act runs to three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 该法对濒危物种的界定有三页之长。
senses.why: law cannot leave a key term vague, so the everyday phrase is given a precise statutory wording.
senses.whyCN: 法律不能让关键术语含糊，因此给这个日常短语配上了精确的法定措辞。

intro.en: The phrase pairs an English adjective built on danger with Latin species 'kind, appearance'. Species comes from specere 'to look'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把基于 danger 的英语形容词与拉丁 species「种类、外观」并列。species 出自 specere「看」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Species in Latin meant 'a look, an appearance, a kind'; it was a fifth-declension noun and already covered both singular and plural uses.
items.cn: 拉丁 species 意为「外观、样子、种类」，属第五变格法名词，当时已兼有单数与复数用法。

items.en: The noun rests on specere 'to look, to see', the same root that gives spectacle, inspect and specimen.
items.cn: 这个名词基于 specere「看、观察」，同一词根也给出 spectacle、inspect 与 specimen。

items.en: English adopted species in the sixteenth century, and its biological sense was fixed by Linnaeus in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪吸收 species，其生物学义由林奈在 18 世纪固定。

items.en: The fixed phrase emerged in the 1960s; the United States passed an Endangered Species Preservation Act in 1966 and the Endangered Species Act in 1973.
items.cn: 这一固定短语在 1960 年代出现；美国 1966 年通过《濒危物种保存法》，1973 年通过《濒危物种法》。

items.en: The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, signed in 1973, carried the phrase into international law.
items.cn: 1973 年签署的《濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约》把这个短语带入国际法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of the full phrase is not precisely recorded, and the deeper origin of Latin specere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：完整短语的最早印刷记录没有确切定论；拉丁 specere 的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the risk labels that are stacked in a fixed order and constantly swapped; group two holds ways of naming rarity or protection.
note.cn: 第一组是按固定次序叠放、常被替换的风险标签；第二组是命名稀有或受保护的其他说法。

entries.definition: In United States law, a species likely to become endangered in the near future; it is less severe than endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 在美国法律中指很可能在近期变为濒危的物种；严重程度低于 endangered。

entries.definition: A species at risk because of small numbers or narrow range, but not yet in danger of imminent extinction.
entries.definitionCN: 因数量少或分布窄而受威胁、但尚未面临迫近灭绝的物种。

entries.definition: A species facing an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild immediately; it sits above endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指在野外面临极高、迫近灭绝风险的物种；等级高于 endangered。

entries.definition: A species with no living members; it has passed beyond the endangered stage altogether.
entries.definitionCN: 指已无存活个体的物种；已完全越过濒危阶段。

entries.definition: A species with few individuals or a small range; rarity alone does not make it endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体少或分布窄的物种；仅稀有并不等于濒危。

entries.definition: A species covered by protective law; the protection may exist for reasons other than extinction risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指受保护法覆盖的物种；保护理由未必是灭绝风险。

entries.definition: An informal cover term for any species in trouble, including those not yet formally listed.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何处境不佳的物种，包括尚未正式列名者。

entries.definition: A species picked for campaigns because it draws public support; it need not itself be endangered.
entries.definitionCN: 指为宣传而选出的物种，因其能带来公众支持；本身未必濒危。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: endangered 'in danger' + species 'kind': a kind that is in danger of ending.
normal.cn: endangered「处于危险」+ species「种类」：一种面临终结危险的生物。

normal.en: The family runs endanger, endangered, endangerment, species, speciation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 endanger、endangered、endangerment、species、speciation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal sense: endangered species list, endangered species act, trade in endangered species.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律义：濒危物种名录、濒危物种法、濒危物种贸易。

normal.en: Species is both singular and plural, so the phrase never becomes endangered speciess.
normal.cn: species 单复数同形，因此这个短语绝不会写成 endangered speciess。

normal.en: The ladder runs vulnerable, endangered, critically endangered, extinct in the wild, extinct.
normal.cn: 等级阶梯依次为易危、濒危、极危、野外灭绝、灭绝。

abstract.en: Picture a list where each name has an empty chair beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份名录，每个名字旁边都有一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a poster animal that stands in for a thousand unnamed others.
abstract.cn: 想象一只海报上的动物，替千千万万无名者出场。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshop treated as a kind of animal that may vanish.
abstract.cn: 想象一家书店被当成可能消失的一种动物。

examples.en: Endangered species are often concentrated in a few small habitats.
examples.cn: 濒危物种往往集中在少数狭小的生境里。

examples.en: The act requires a plan for every endangered species it lists.
examples.cn: 该法要求为每一个列名的濒危物种制定计划。

examples.en: Smuggling endangered species is treated as a serious crime.
examples.cn: 走私濒危物种被视为重罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「endangered（身处危险）+ species（物种）」——面临消失的物种 → 濒危物种

root: endangered（en- + danger + -ed，danger 经古法语 dangier 源自通俗拉丁 dominiarium「领主之权」）+ 拉丁 species「种类、外观」（出自 specere「看」）。英语 endangered species。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one label: a kind of living thing is marked as at risk, and the label is then read as a warning, a legal status, a rank, a trend, a poster, a budget line and finally a metaphor for anything vanishing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个标签展开：某一类生物被标记为有风险，这个标签再被读成警告、法律身份、等级、趋势、海报、预算条目，最后成为任何「正在消失之物」的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of names, each with an empty chair beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份名字清单，每个名字旁都有一把空椅子。

branches.en: DECLINE ITSELF: whether already few or still many but falling, the risk is the defining feature.
branches.cn: 下降本身：无论已经很少还是仍多但在下滑，风险都是界定特征。

branches.en: LEGAL STATUS: a condition becomes a listable status with duties attached.
branches.cn: 法律身份：一种状况变成可列名的身份，并附带义务。

branches.en: RANK AND POSTER: the label is both a rung on a ladder and a face on a campaign.
branches.cn: 等级与海报：这个标签既是阶梯上的一档，也是宣传中的一张脸。

branches.en: POLICY OBJECT: money and programmes are attached to the category, not to one animal.
branches.cn: 政策对象：资金与计划附着在这一类别，而非某一只动物。

branches.en: BORROWED METAPHOR: any vanishing type can be called an endangered species.
branches.cn: 借用的隐喻：任何正在消失的类型都可被称为濒危物种。

intro.en: The phrase joins an English adjective of risk to a Latin noun of kind; the two halves come from different language families and keep their own histories.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示风险的英语形容词接到表示种类的拉丁名词上；两半来自不同语系，各自保留自己的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin species yields English species, speciation and specimen, while the adjective half comes through French from Latin dominus 'lord'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species 衍生英语 species、speciation 与 specimen；形容词那一半则经法语来自拉丁 dominus「领主」。

items.example: The prefix makes a verb of putting.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀造出「使进入」的动词。

items.example: The danger was past by dawn.
The colony is endangered by warming water.
items.exampleCN: 该群落受水温上升威胁。

items.meaning: a kind at risk of ending
items.example: Every endangered species on the list has a plan.
items.exampleCN: 名录上的每个濒危物种都有计划。

items.example: Speciation followed the river's change of course.
items.exampleCN: 河流改道之后出现了物种形成。

items.example: The specimen was pressed and labelled.
items.exampleCN: 标本被压平并贴了标签。

items.meaning: the state of being at risk
items.example: Endangerment of the species was documented in 1990.
items.exampleCN: 该物种的濒危状态在 1990 年被记录。

items.example: A specious argument looks sound and is not.
items.exampleCN: 似是而非的论证看起来成立，其实不然。

definition_zh: 蓝移；光谱线整体向短波方向的移动
definition_en: the displacement of spectral lines toward shorter wavelengths, caused by motion toward the observer or by light falling into a gravitational well
core_image: 光谱图上，一条条谱线离开原位，向蓝色一端挤过去
scene: 观测者把同一颗星的两次曝光叠在一起，发现谱线这次整体向左挪到了蓝色一端。 An approaching star produces a slight blueshift in its spectral lines.
sceneCN: 这里指「谱线整体向短波一端移动的现象」（第 1 个义项：波长被压缩、频率升高）；句意为正在接近的恒星使其谱线出现轻微蓝移。图中可辨识物件：两次曝光底片、谱线、比对尺、观测椅。

pos.zh: 蓝移；向短波方向的谱线位移

senses.title: Spectral lines moved toward blue
senses.titleCN: 谱线整体向短波一端移动
senses.definition: the shift of spectral lines to shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 谱线向更短波长、更高频率的移动
senses.example: An approaching star produces a slight blueshift in its spectral lines.
senses.exampleCN: 正在接近的恒星使其谱线出现轻微蓝移。
senses.why: blue names the end of the visible spectrum that the lines move toward, and shift names the displacement.
senses.whyCN: blue 指谱线移向的可见光谱那一端，shift 指位移本身。

senses.title: Doppler blueshift from approach
senses.titleCN: 接近运动造成的多普勒蓝移
senses.definition: the blueshift produced when a source moves toward the observer
senses.definitionCN: 光源朝观测者运动时产生的蓝移
senses.example: The star's blueshift shows that it is falling toward us.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星的蓝移表明它正朝我们靠近。
senses.why: an approaching source crowds the waves it sends, so the cause is motion and the effect is shorter wavelength.
senses.whyCN: 接近的光源把发出的波挤紧，因此成因是运动，结果是波长变短。

senses.title: Gravitational blueshift
senses.definition: the blueshift of light falling into a strong gravitational field
senses.definitionCN: 光落入强引力场时产生的蓝移
senses.example: Light falling toward the dense star gained a gravitational blueshift.
senses.exampleCN: 朝致密恒星下落的光获得了引力蓝移。
senses.why: light gains energy as it falls into a well, and higher energy appears at shorter wavelength.
senses.whyCN: 光落入势阱时获得能量，能量变高就表现为波长变短。

senses.title: The measured blueshift value
senses.definition: the number recording a fractional wavelength decrease, often written as a negative z
senses.definitionCN: 记录波长相对减少量的数值，常写作负的 z
senses.example: The measured blueshift was tiny, a fraction of a nanometre.
senses.exampleCN: 测得的蓝移极小，只有一纳米的一小部分。
senses.why: a value is needed for comparison, so the word also names the number, conventionally negative.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要一个数值，因此这个词也指那个数，惯例上取负值。

senses.title: A blueshifted line
senses.definition: a particular absorption or emission line found at a shorter wavelength than its laboratory position
senses.definitionCN: 出现在比实验室位置更短波长处的某条吸收线或发射线
senses.example: The blueshifted absorption line revealed hot gas moving outward.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝移的吸收线揭示出正在外流的高温气体。
senses.why: the adjective form fixes the phenomenon to individual lines, which is what observers actually measure.
senses.whyCN: 形容词形式把现象落实到一条条谱线上，而观测者测量的正是这些线。

senses.title: The counterpart of redshift
senses.definition: the opposite sign of the same displacement, used whenever sources approach or space contracts locally
senses.definitionCN: 同一位移的相反方向，用于光源接近或局部空间收缩的情形
senses.example: In the pair, one galaxy shows blueshift and the other redshift.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一对星系中，一个显示蓝移，另一个显示红移。
senses.why: redshift and blueshift name one axis in two directions, so the terms are defined against each other.
senses.whyCN: 红移与蓝移是同一条轴上的两个方向，因此这两个术语互为定义。

senses.title: Blueshift in stellar and galactic observation
senses.titleCN: 恒星与星系观测中的蓝移
senses.definition: a blueshift used to identify infalling gas, rotating companions or approaching clusters
senses.definitionCN: 用于识别内落气体、旋转伴星或接近星团的蓝移
senses.example: The blueshift of the companion star exposed the binary's orbital motion.
senses.exampleCN: 伴星的蓝移揭示了这对双星的轨道运动。
senses.why: because motion is common in binaries and clusters, blueshift became a standard diagnostic.
senses.whyCN: 由于双星与星团中运动普遍，蓝移成了标准的诊断手段。

senses.title: Figurative compression or advance
senses.definition: a borrowed use for any signal that arrives compressed, raised or early
senses.definitionCN: 借指任何到达时被压缩、被抬高或提前的信号
senses.example: The remastered track has a kind of blueshift: everything sounds tighter and higher.
senses.exampleCN: 重制后的曲目有种蓝移感：一切都更紧、更高。
senses.why: the physical crowding of waves became an image for anything that reaches us speeded up.
senses.whyCN: 波被物理挤紧，成了任何抵达时被加速的事物的意象。

intro.en: Blueshift is an English compound formed in astronomy from blue and shift. It has no Latin ancestor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: blueshift 是英语复合词，在天文学中由 blue 与 shift 构成，没有拉丁语祖先。年代均为约数。

items.en: Blue descends from Old French bleu, itself from a Germanic source; shift goes back to Old English sciftan 'to arrange, divide'.
items.cn: blue 来自古法语 bleu，而 bleu 又出自日耳曼语来源；shift 可追溯到古英语 sciftan「安排、分配」。

items.en: The compound appeared in the twentieth century as the natural partner of redshift, once spectra were measured precisely enough.
items.cn: 这个复合词在二十世纪出现，作为红移的天然对应词，当时光谱已能被足够精确地测量。

items.en: Studies of binary stars and galaxy clusters gave the term a working role in measuring motion.
items.cn: 对双星与星系团的研究，使这个词在测量运动方面有了实际用途。

items.en: Relativity added the gravitational blueshift, extending the word beyond motion alone.
items.cn: 相对论增添了引力蓝移，把这个词扩展到运动之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest printed use of the compound is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic origin of blue is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个复合词最早的印刷用例没有定论，blue 在日耳曼语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the mirror-image terms that are routinely confused; group two holds the physical quantities involved.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的镜像术语；第二组是所涉的物理量。

entries.definition: Displacement toward longer wavelengths, caused by recession, expansion or light climbing out of a well.
entries.definitionCN: 向更长波长的位移，由退行、膨胀或光爬出势阱造成。

entries.definition: The participial adjective for lines that have already moved; the noun names the phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 谱线已经移动的分词形容词；名词形式才指现象本身。

entries.definition: The colour itself; in the compound it only marks the direction of the shift.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色本身；在复合词中只标记位移的方向。

entries.definition: Any displacement at all; blueshift adds the spectral setting and the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 任何位移；blueshift 增添了光谱语境与方向。

entries.definition: The general frequency change from relative motion; blueshift is its short-wavelength half.
entries.definitionCN: 相对运动造成的一般频率变化；蓝移是其中短波的一半。

entries.definition: Moving nearer, the usual cause of an observed blueshift.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近的运动，是观测到蓝移的常见成因。

entries.definition: The squeezing of waves that raises frequency; blueshift is its spectral signature.
entries.definitionCN: 波被挤紧从而提高频率；蓝移是其光谱特征。

entries.definition: The distance between crests; a blueshift is a decrease in this distance.
entries.definitionCN: 波峰之间的距离；蓝移就是这一距离的缩短。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real observations and real paired terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实观测与真实成对术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Blue plus shift: lines slide toward the blue end.
normal.cn: 蓝色加位移：谱线滑向蓝端。

normal.en: Approaching sources blueshift; receding sources redshift.
normal.cn: 接近的光源蓝移；远离的光源红移。

normal.en: Falling into a gravity well also produces a blueshift.
normal.cn: 落入引力势阱同样产生蓝移。

normal.en: A blueshift is a negative z on the same scale as redshift.
normal.cn: 蓝移与红移在同一标尺上取负的 z。

normal.en: Binary stars reveal their orbital motion through alternating red and blue shifts.
normal.cn: 双星通过交替的红移与蓝移显露轨道运动。

abstract.en: Picture a spring being compressed so the coils sit closer together.
abstract.cn: 想象弹簧被压紧，线圈彼此靠近。

abstract.en: Picture an ambulance growing higher in pitch as it rushes toward you.
abstract.cn: 想象救护车冲向你时音调越来越高。

abstract.en: Picture a message that arrives shorter and quicker than it was sent.
abstract.cn: 想象一条消息抵达时比发出时更短、更快。

examples.en: The blueshift of the gas cloud showed that it was falling inward.
examples.cn: 气体云的蓝移表明它正向内落。

examples.en: A negative z records a blueshift rather than a redshift.
examples.cn: 负的 z 记录的是蓝移而非红移。

examples.en: The two stars trade blueshift and redshift as they orbit.
examples.cn: 两颗星在轨道上交替呈现蓝移与红移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blue（蓝）+ shift（移动）」——谱线整体往蓝端移动 → 蓝移

root: 英语复合词，由 blue（经古法语 bleu，出自日耳曼语）与 shift（古英语 sciftan）构成，二十世纪在天文学中造出，无拉丁同族，拉丁条目数组留空；blue 的日耳曼语之前来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one compression: lines crowd blue, a source approaches, gravity pulls light down, a value is read, a line is identified, the term pairs with redshift, observations use it and finally any signal arrives speeded up.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次压缩：谱线向蓝端挤、光源接近、引力把光拉下、读出数值、指认谱线、与红移成对、用于观测，最后是任何信号抵达时已被加速。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spectrum squeezed from the red end so that every line slides toward blue.
core.cn: 核心意象：光谱被从红端挤紧，每条谱线都滑向蓝端。

branches.en: ONE AXIS, TWO SIGNS: the same displacement read in the opposite direction.
branches.cn: 一条轴、两个符号：同一位移的相反方向。

branches.en: MOTION TOWARD US: approach crowds the waves and betrays orbital motion.
branches.cn: 朝我们的运动：接近把波挤紧，也泄露轨道运动。

branches.en: FALLING LIGHT: gravity, not speed, supplies the compression.
branches.cn: 下落的光：压缩来自引力，而非速度。

branches.en: VALUE AND LINE: the effect is read as a negative number on a named line.
branches.cn: 数值与谱线：效应读成负值，落在一条具名的线上。

branches.en: METAPHOR: anything that arrives tighter and higher borrows the image.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何抵达时更紧、更高的事物都借用这一意象。

intro.en: Blueshift is a two-word English compound whose halves are both ordinary words, so its meaning is fully transparent.
intro.cn: blueshift 是由两个普通英语词构成的复合词，两半都是常用词，因此意义完全透明。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: blue reached English through French from a Germanic source, and shift is native Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁条目：blue 经法语来自日耳曼语来源，shift 则是本族古英语词。

items.structure: Old French bleu, from a Germanic source
items.meaning: the colour of the clear sky
items.example: The line sits at the blue end.
The blueshift was easy to see.

items.meaning: the process of moving toward blue
items.example: The blueshifting of the gas continued.
The companion showed a redshift instead.
A blue filter isolates the short waves.
items.exampleCN: 蓝色滤光片分离出短波。

items.example: The star has a bluish tint.
A small shift changed the result.
items.exampleCN: 微小的位移改变了结果。

definition_zh: 可持续性；可持续；（组织、财政等）长期可维持性；可持续发展理念
definition_en: the quality of being able to continue over the long term without exhausting the resources or conditions it depends on
core_image: 一根幼苗被下方的木桩托住，旁边一只天平两端分别放着今天的收成与留给来年的种子
scene: 这里指「可持续性」。 The city's sustainability program cut energy use by a fifth within three years.
sceneCN: 这里 sustainability 是「机构层面的可持续战略」（第 5 个义项：城市作为治理主体对长期环境目标的管理）；句意：这座城市的可持续计划在三年内把能耗降低了五分之一。图中可辨识物件：被木桩托住的幼苗、天平、收成堆、种子袋、下降的能耗曲线。

pos.zh: 可持续性；可持续；（生态系统、组织、财政等的）长期可维持性；（指理念或事业时多不可数）

forms.label: 复数（指多种可持续性指标或做法）

derivatives.zh: 维持；支撑（sustain 源自古法语 sustenir，再上溯拉丁 sustinere = sub-「自下」+ tenere「握住」）
可持续的（sustain + -able「可……的」，义项由「可被支撑」偏移为「可长期维持」）
食物；生计（sustain + -ance「……之物」，由「支撑」偏移为「维持生命之物」）
不可持续的（un-「不」+ sustainable，语义偏移为「继续下去会崩溃的」）

senses.title: The ability of an ecosystem to endure
senses.titleCN: 生态可持续性：生态系统长期存续的能力
senses.definition: the capacity of an ecosystem to keep producing and renewing itself over time without collapsing
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统在长期内持续产出、自我更新而不崩溃的能力
senses.example: The reef's sustainability depends on water temperature and the balance of species.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的可持续性取决于水温与物种平衡。
senses.why: Here the word answers a question about nature: can this system keep going on its own? The sense of holding up from below becomes the ecosystem holding itself up across generations.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词回答一个关于自然的问题：这个系统能否自行持续运转？「从下方托住」的本义转化为生态系统跨世代自我支撑的能力。

senses.title: A system or enterprise that can keep functioning
senses.titleCN: 系统或组织的可维持性：长期运转而不瓦解
senses.definition: the ability of an organization, project or technical system to continue operating within its resources over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 组织、项目或技术系统在其资源范围内长期持续运转的能力
senses.example: Without new funding, the program's sustainability is in doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 没有新的资金，该项目的可持续性堪忧。
senses.why: The same question is asked of human institutions: a project is sustainable if it can renew its resources, staff and purpose instead of living on one grant. The image is a machine that fuels itself.
senses.whyCN: 同样的问题被问到人类组织上：一个项目若能不断补充资源、人手与目标，而不是靠一笔拨款过活，就是可持续的。意象是一台能自我供能的机器。

senses.title: Public finances that can be serviced indefinitely
senses.titleCN: 财政可持续性：债务能被长期偿付
senses.definition: the condition of government debt and spending that can be maintained without defaulting or forcing intolerable future burdens
senses.definitionCN: 政府债务与支出能够长期维持、不致违约或给未来造成难以承受负担的状态
senses.example: Fiscal sustainability requires debt to grow no faster than the economy.
senses.exampleCN: 财政可持续性要求债务增长不快于经济增长。
senses.why: Economists transferred the word to public accounts: a fiscal path is sustainable if it can be serviced year after year. The holding up becomes the state holding up its own obligations.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这个词转用到公共账目：一条财政路径若能年复一年地偿付，就是可持续的。「托住」变成了国家托住自己的债务义务。

senses.title: Development that does not spend the future
senses.titleCN: 可持续发展：不透支未来的发展
senses.definition: economic and social progress that meets present needs without preventing future generations from meeting theirs
senses.definitionCN: 满足当代需求、又不损害后代满足其需求能力的经济社会发展
senses.example: The master plan links housing, transport and industry under the banner of sustainability.
senses.exampleCN: 总体规划把住房、交通与工业统一在可持续性的旗帜下。
senses.why: The 1987 Brundtland report made sustainable development a global slogan; sustainability became the noun that names the whole project of balancing growth with the planet's limits.
senses.whyCN: 1987 年的《布伦特兰报告》使可持续发展成为全球口号；sustainability 成为命名「在增长与地球极限之间求平衡」这一整套事业的抽象名词。

senses.title: A company's long-term environmental and social strategy
senses.titleCN: 企业可持续战略：企业层面的长期环境与社会管理
senses.definition: the policies and reporting through which a business manages its environmental and social impact over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 企业用以长期管理其环境与社会影响的政策与信息披露
senses.example: The bank made sustainability a board-level responsibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行把可持续性列为董事会层面的职责。
senses.why: From the 1990s companies turned the movement's demand into a management practice, with sustainability reports, officers and targets. The word now names an organizational discipline.
senses.whyCN: 自二十世纪九十年代起，企业把运动的诉求变成管理实践，出现了可持续发展报告、负责人与目标。该词如今命名一种组织化的专业领域。

senses.title: Farming and food that last
senses.titleCN: 农业与粮食体系的可持续性
senses.definition: the quality of agricultural practices and food supply chains that preserve soil, water and livelihoods for the long term
senses.definitionCN: 能够长期保住土壤、水源与生计的农业做法与粮食供应链的性质
senses.example: Soil erosion is the biggest threat to the farm's sustainability.
senses.exampleCN: 水土流失是对该农场可持续性的最大威胁。
senses.why: Applied to agriculture, the word measures a system's ability to keep producing without mining its own soil. It is sustainability with the ground under it made literal.
senses.whyCN: 用在农业上，这个词衡量一个体系能否在不耗尽自己土地的前提下持续产出。这是把「脚下有支撑」变成字面意义的可持续性。

senses.title: A research field that studies endurance
senses.titleCN: 可持续性科学：研究长期存续的交叉学科
senses.definition: the interdisciplinary study of how natural and social systems can meet human needs over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 研究自然系统与社会系统如何长期满足人类需求的交叉学科
senses.example: Sustainability science draws on ecology, economics and engineering together.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续性科学同时借用生态学、经济学与工程学。
senses.why: Around the year 2000 the word became the name of a discipline that treats endurance as a technical problem; the noun shifted from a quality to a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 大约在 2000 年前后，该词成为一个学科的名称，把「长期存续」当作技术问题来研究；名词从一种性质变成一门学问。

senses.title: A lifestyle a person can actually keep up
senses.titleCN: 生活方式的可持续性：个人能否长期坚持
senses.definition: the quality of a habit, budget or way of living that a person can maintain without burning out or giving up
senses.definitionCN: 一个人能够长期坚持、不致耗尽精力或放弃的习惯、预算或生活方式的性质
senses.example: Running every day sounds admirable, but sustainability matters more than intensity.
senses.exampleCN: 每天跑步听起来值得敬佩，但能否长期坚持比强度更重要。
senses.why: Health writers borrowed the word: a plan is sustainable if the person can repeat it next month. The scale has shrunk from the planet to one daily routine.
senses.whyCN: 健康类作者借用这个词：一个人下个月还能照做的计划才是可持续的。尺度从整个地球缩小到一项日常作息。

intro.en: Sustainability is the noun sustainable plus the quality ending -ity; sustainable is built on sustain, taken through Old French sustenir from Latin sustinere, made of sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: sustainability 是形容词 sustainable 加性质词尾 -ity 构成；sustainable 建立在 sustain 之上，后者经古法语 sustenir 源自拉丁 sustinere，由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」组成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sustinere 'to hold up from below, support, endure' was built on sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. Its original picture is of taking weight from underneath and keeping it in place.
items.cn: 拉丁 sustinere「自下托住、支撑、承受」由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」构成。其原始画面是从下方接住重量并让它保持原位。

items.en: English took sustain through Old French sustenir in the medieval period, with the meanings 'to keep in being, maintain, provide for'.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪经古法语 sustenir 借入 sustain，义为「使存续、维持、供养」。

items.en: The adjective sustainable, formed on sustain with -able, meant in the seventeenth century 'able to be supported or maintained', used of arguments, weights and provisions. Its first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 sustainable 由 sustain 加 -able 构成，十七世纪时义为「可被支撑或维持的」，用于论证、重物与给养。其最早书证年代存疑。

items.en: In the 1970s and 1980s sustainable was applied to development, energy and agriculture that do not exhaust resources, and the phrase sustainable development became a global policy term after the 1987 Brundtland report.
items.cn: 二十世纪七八十年代，sustainable 被用于不耗尽资源的开发、能源与农业；sustainable development 一词在 1987 年《布伦特兰报告》后成为全球政策用语。

items.en: Sustainability adds -ity, the ending of quality. The noun existed earlier in the general sense 'capability of being maintained' (first citation uncertain) and spread as a movement term in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: sustainability 加上了性质词尾 -ity。该名词更早便以「可被维持的能力」这一一般义存在（最早书证年代存疑），二十世纪后期作为运动用语普及。

items.en: The exact first English citations of both sustainable and sustainability are uncertain. The deeper root of tenere is generally taken to be reconstructed Indo-European *ten- 'to stretch, hold', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 首见年代存疑：sustainable 与 sustainability 的英语最早书证年代均不确定。tenere 的更深词根一般认为是重构的印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」，属重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the sustain family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for lasting without exhausting what keeps something going.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 sustain 词族；第二组给出表示「不耗尽支撑物而长久延续」的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective: able to be kept going. Sustainability is the noun that names the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指可长期维持的；sustainability 是命名这一性质的名词。

entries.definition: The verb of keeping something going or holding it up. Sustainable describes the thing; sustain is the action.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指维持或托住某物；sustainable 描述事物，sustain 是动作。

entries.definition: Continuous over time. Sustained describes an effort that did keep going; sustainable asks whether it can keep going without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续的；sustained 描述确实一直持续的努力，sustainable 追问它能否无损害地持续下去。

entries.definition: The food or means that keeps a life going. It is the concrete thing; sustainability is the abstract quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指维持生命的食物或手段，是具体之物；sustainability 是抽象性质。

entries.definition: Resistance to wear over time. Durability is about lasting physically; sustainability is about not exhausting what keeps something going.
entries.definitionCN: 指对磨损的抵抗力：durability 强调物理上耐用，sustainability 强调不耗尽维持其运转的东西。

entries.definition: The ability to work or succeed. A plan can be viable now yet unsustainable over decades.
entries.definitionCN: 指行得通、能成功的能力；一个方案眼下可行（viable），却可能在数十年内不可持续。

entries.definition: The ability to recover from shocks. Resilience is about bouncing back; sustainability is about not being driven to the point of collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 指从冲击中恢复的能力：resilience 强调反弹回来，sustainability 强调不被逼到崩溃边缘。

entries.definition: The quality of a resource that regenerates. Renewability feeds sustainability, but a system can be renewable yet still mismanaged.
entries.definitionCN: 指资源再生的性质：renewability 为 sustainability 提供基础，但系统可再生（renewable）仍可能被管理失当。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sustain + -able + -ity: hold it up from below, say it can be kept up, then name the quality.
normal.cn: sustain + -able + -ity：先从下方托住，再说「撑得住」，最后为这一性质命名。

normal.en: The family runs sustain, sustainable, sustainability, sustained, sustenance, unsustainable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sustain、sustainable、sustainability、sustained、sustenance、unsustainable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the movement: sustainable development, corporate sustainability, fiscal sustainability, sustainability report.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一运动领域：可持续发展、企业可持续性、财政可持续性、可持续发展报告。

normal.en: A fishing quota is sustainable only if the catch does not exceed what regrows.
normal.cn: 只有当渔获不超过再生长量时，捕捞配额才是可持续的。

normal.en: Sustain is the verb, sustainable the adjective, sustainability the noun: the same act at three distances.
normal.cn: sustain 是动词，sustainable 是形容词，sustainability 是名词：同一个动作的三种距离。

abstract.en: Picture a sapling held upright by a stake, still growing season after season.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵被木桩扶正的幼苗，一季又一季地生长。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger that stays balanced year after year, never dipping into the red.
abstract.cn: 想象一本年复一年保持平衡、从不出现赤字的账本。

abstract.en: Picture a forest that gives timber every decade without shrinking.
abstract.cn: 想象一片每十年都能产出木材却不见缩小的森林。

examples.en: The company's sustainability report lists emissions for each factory.
examples.cn: 这家公司的可持续发展报告列出了每家工厂的排放量。

examples.en: Fiscal sustainability forces governments to think beyond the next election.
examples.cn: 财政可持续性迫使政府把眼光放到下一次选举之后。

examples.en: Scientists warn that groundwater use is far beyond sustainability.
examples.cn: 科学家警告，地下水开采已远远超出可持续的范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sustain（维持）+ able + ity」——托得住、撑得久 → sustainability 可持续性

root: 拉丁 sustinere = sub-「自下」+ tenere「握住、保持」→ 古法语 sustenir → 英语 sustain + -able + -ity。更深词根一般认为是印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses ask the same question at different scales: can an ecosystem, an organization, a budget, a development path, a company, a farm, a discipline or a daily habit keep going?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同尺度上提出同一个问题：生态系统、组织、预算、发展路径、企业、农场、学科或日常习惯，能否一直运转下去？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load is held up from below so it can keep going without breaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：重物被从下方托住，得以持续运转而不垮。

branches.en: NATURAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY: ecosystems and institutions keep functioning over time.
branches.cn: 自然与组织能力：生态系统与机构长期保持运转。

branches.en: PUBLIC FINANCE AND DEVELOPMENT: debt stays serviceable and growth does not spend its own base.
branches.cn: 公共财政与发展：债务可偿付，增长不消耗自身根基。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL STRATEGY: companies and cities manage resources for the long term.
branches.cn: 机构战略：企业与城市为长期而管理资源。

branches.en: AGRICULTURE AND SCIENCE: food systems and research disciplines treat endurance as a measurable object.
branches.cn: 农业与科学：粮食体系与研究学科把「存续」当作可测量的对象。

branches.en: PERSONAL ENDURANCE: a habit or lifestyle can be repeated without burning out.
branches.cn: 个人耐力：习惯或生活方式可反复执行而不致耗尽。

intro.en: Sustainability is layered: the Latin verb sustinere 'hold up from below', the adjective suffix -able, and the quality-noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: sustainability 是分层的：拉丁动词 sustinere「自下托住」、形容词词尾 -able、性质名词词尾 -ity。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is tenere 'to hold, keep' with the prefix sub- 'from below'; -able came through French from Latin -abilis, and -ity from Latin -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 tenere「握住、保持」加前缀 sub-「自下」；-able 经法语源自拉丁 -abilis，-ity 源自拉丁 -itas。

items.meaning: the quality of being maintainable over the long term
items.example: Urban planners debated the sustainability of the new district.
items.exampleCN: 城市规划者讨论了新区的可持续性。

items.meaning: to hold up, keep in being, maintain
items.example: The land can sustain only a few thousand people.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地只能养活几千人。

items.meaning: able to be continued without exhausting the base
items.meaningCN: 可持续的；不耗尽根基而能继续的
items.example: They looked for a sustainable source of water.
items.exampleCN: 他们寻找可持续的水源。

items.meaning: the food or means that keeps life going
items.meaningCN: 维持生命的食物或手段
items.example: The migrants lived on scant sustenance.
items.exampleCN: 这些迁徙者靠微薄的食物维生。

items.meaning: unable to be continued without collapse
items.meaningCN: 不可持续的；继续下去会崩溃的
items.exampleCN: 债务水平被证明不可持续。

items.meaning: able to be held or defended
items.example: His argument is no longer tenable.
The treaty lets members retain control of their waters.
items.exampleCN: 条约允许成员国保留对其水域的控制。

items.structure: Latin manu tenere (to hold in hand) via Old French
items.meaning: to keep in good condition or working order
items.example: Regular checks maintain the bridge in safe condition.
items.exampleCN: 定期检查让桥梁保持安全状态。

definition_en: difficult to catch, find, understand or achieve

scene: 雾里一只蝴蝶停在叶尖，男孩把网兜慢慢合拢，它却从网眼边滑走了。 An elusive butterfly slipped out of the closing net.

pos.zh: 难捉摸的；难懂的；难找到的

senses.title: Hard to catch
senses.definition: difficult to catch, find or reach
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以抓住、找到或够到
senses.example: The leopard proved elusive, and the camera traps recorded only leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 那只豹子始终难以捕捉，红外相机只拍到了树叶。
senses.why: A butterfly leaving the net at the exact moment the rim closes
senses.whyCN: 网口合拢的那一刻蝴蝶离开网兜

senses.title: Hard to define
senses.definition: difficult to describe or understand precisely
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以准确描述或理解
senses.example: Happiness is an elusive concept that no survey can pin down.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福是个难以界定的概念，任何问卷都抓不住它。
senses.why: Sugar dissolving in a closed hand before the fingers can hold it
senses.whyCN: 糖在合拢的手心里化掉，手指还来不及握住

senses.definition: difficult to remember or to achieve
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）难以回想起来或难以达成

senses.exampleCN: 旋律早就想起来了，歌名却迟迟记不起。

intro.en: Elusive comes from Latin e- meaning out and ludere meaning to play; eludere is to escape by slipping away, like a fish that leaves the hands.
intro.cn: elusive 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 ludere（玩耍）；eludere 意为靠滑脱逃身，像一条从手中溜走的鱼。

items.en: Ludere means to play, and gives English illusion and allusion.
items.cn: ludere 意为玩耍，给出英语 illusion 与 allusion。

items.en: Eludere means to escape or to mock, built from e- plus ludere.
items.cn: eludere 意为逃脱或戏弄，由 e- 加 ludere 构成。

items.en: Elusus is the past participle, meaning slipped away or escaped.
items.cn: elusus 是过去分词，意为溜走或逃脱。

items.en: English forms elusive from elusus on the pattern of abusive and delusive.
items.cn: 英语按 abusive 与 delusive 的构词模式，由 elusus 造出 elusive。

items.en: The noun elusiveness appears in criticism and in philosophy.
items.cn: 名词 elusiveness 出现在批评与哲学文字中。

items.en: Elusive spreads to targets, memories and results that stay out of reach.
items.cn: elusive 扩展到始终够不着的目标、记忆与结果。

note.en: Elusive, elude and illusion share the Latin root ludere, to play; evasive and intangible are the nearest everyday synonyms.
note.cn: elusive、elude 与 illusion 共享拉丁词根 ludere（玩耍）；evasive 与 intangible 是最接近的日常同义词。

entries.definitionCN: 逃避；使困惑

entries.definition: a false impression of what is real
entries.definitionCN: 幻觉；错觉

entries.definition: containing an indirect reference

entries.definition: tending to avoid a direct answer
entries.definitionCN: 回避的；闪烁其词的

dict_mnemonic.text: elusive ＝ e-（向外）＋ lus（玩耍，拉丁 ludere，过去分词 elusus「溜走」）＋ -ive（形容词后缀）＝「像玩一样溜出去的」。动词 elude 逃避、使困惑，副词 elusively，名词 elusiveness；同根 illusion 幻觉、allusion 典故、delude 欺骗。三类用法：抓不住 an elusive butterfly 难捕捉的蝴蝶、an elusive criminal 在逃的罪犯；说不清 an elusive concept 难以界定的概念、an elusive meaning 捉摸不定的含义；够不着 an elusive goal 难以实现的目标、elusive memory 想不起的记忆。常与 remain、prove 连用：remain elusive 仍然难以捉摸。比较级用 more elusive，没有 elusiver。近义 evasive 侧重故意回避，intangible 侧重无形，slippery 侧重滑脱；elusive 强调你越追它越溜。注意与 allusive（用典的）只差一个字母。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ ludere（玩耍）→ eludere（逃脱）→ elusus（溜走的）→ elusive（难捉摸的）

sensesIntro.en: Three things that leave the hand: a butterfly at the closing net, sugar dissolving in a fist and a name stepping back from the tip of the tongue.
sensesIntro.cn: 三样从手里溜走的东西：网口合拢时的蝴蝶、拳头里化掉的糖，以及从舌尖退回去的名字。
