intro.en: Elusive is e- plus lus- plus -ive; the verb elude drops -ive, -ly gives elusively and -ness gives elusiveness.
intro.cn: elusive 由 e- 加 lus- 加 -ive 组成；动词 elude 去掉 -ive，-ly 给出 elusively，-ness 给出 elusiveness。

latinIntro.en: Latin ludere means to play, eludere to escape and illusio a mocking; these give elusive, illusion and delude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为玩耍，eludere 意为逃脱，illusio 意为戏弄；这些给出 elusive、illusion 与 delude。

definition_zh: 废除；废止（法律、协议、惯例）
definition_en: to repeal or abolish a law, agreement, or custom formally
core_image: 一纸判词把旧条文划掉作废
scene: 议长敲下木槌，宣布那条过时的税法从今天起不再有效。 The new government abrogated the decades-old treaty.
sceneCN: 这里 abrogate 是「废除」（第 1 个义项：新政府废除旧条约）；句意为新政府废除了那项数十年之久的条约。

pos.zh: 废除；废止；撤销

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「废除；废止」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有废除权的；废止性的」
同根近形词，义为「僭取；擅夺」，与废除义无关

senses.title: To repeal a law or agreement formally
senses.definition: to annul or repeal a law, treaty, or contract by formal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由正式权力机关废止或撤销法律、条约或合同
senses.example: Parliament voted to abrogate the emergency decree.
senses.exampleCN: 议会表决废除了那项紧急法令。
senses.why: Latin ab- (away) plus rogare (to propose a law) means to call a law away, cancelling its force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab-（离去）加 rogare（提出法案），义为把法律「召离」，使其失效。

senses.title: To end a practice or obligation
senses.definition: to put an end to an established custom or duty as if repealing it
senses.definitionCN: 像废止法条一样终结既有的惯例或义务
senses.example: The reform abrogated centuries of patronage appointments.
senses.exampleCN: 改革终结了延续数百年的恩惠任命。
senses.why: What custom treated as binding is treated as if it were written law, so the repeal verb extends to it.
senses.whyCN: 惯例本有约束力，被当作成文法对待，废除动词随之延伸至惯例。

intro.en: Abrogate comes from Latin abrogatus, past participle of abrogare 'to repeal', from ab- 'away' and rogare 'to propose a law'.
intro.cn: abrogate 来自拉丁语 abrogatus，是 abrogare「废除」的过去分词，由 ab-「离去」加 rogare「提出法案」构成。

items.en: Rogare meant to ask formally, especially to ask the people to accept a law.
items.cn: rogare 义为正式请求，尤指请求民众接受一项法律。

items.en: In Roman usage, abrogare was the technical term for repealing a statute through vote.
items.cn: 在罗马用法中，abrogare 是经表决废止法规的术语。

items.en: Derogare, by contrast, meant only to subtract part of a law; the pair kept distinct legal senses.
items.cn: 与之相对，derogare 只指削减法律的某部分；两者在法律语中分工明确。

items.en: Subrogare meant to put another law in the place of the repealed one.
items.cn: subrogare 指以另一法条取代被废者。

items.en: The word entered English legal and theological writing with the full Roman sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪该词带着完整的罗马法意义进入英语法律与神学著作。

items.en: It stays formal, reserved for laws, treaties, and solemn institutional acts.
items.cn: 如今仍属正式用语，限于法律、条约与庄严的机构行为。

note.en: The first group gathers the rogare family; the second lists repeal-related verbs.
note.cn: 第一组为 rogare 词族；第二组为表废除的动词。

entries.definition: the act of repealing or the repealed state.
entries.definitionCN: 废除行为或被废状态。

entries.definition: to claim without right; shares the rogare root but means seizing, not repealing.
entries.definitionCN: 僭取；同享 rogare 词根，但义为擅夺而非废除。

entries.definition: to detract from or partially repeal; Roman law partner of abrogate.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损或部分废止；罗马法中与 abrogate 相对。

entries.definition: to question formally; the asking root without the repealing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式质询；同根但只有「问」义。

entries.definition: to give up a throne or duty; looks close but comes from dicere, not rogare.
entries.definitionCN: 放弃王位或职责；形近但词根是 dicere 而非 rogare。

entries.definition: to withdraw a law officially; the everyday legal partner.
entries.definitionCN: 正式撤回法律；日常法律对应词。

entries.definition: to declare something void from the start, as with a marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告自始无效，如宣告婚姻无效。

entries.definition: to cancel a contract or order retroactively.
entries.definitionCN: 追溯性地取消合同或命令。

entries.definition: to confirm formally; the opposite institutional move.
entries.definitionCN: 正式批准；机构行为上的反向操作。

entries.definition: to put a rule back into force after repeal.
entries.definitionCN: 废除后恢复某规则的效力。

normalIntro.en: Use the rogare root and the legal family.
normalIntro.cn: 利用 rogare 词根与法律词族记忆。

normal.en: ab- away + rogare ask-a-law = call the law away.
normal.cn: ab- 离去 + rogare 立法之问 = 把法律召离作废。

normal.en: interrogate asks questions; abrogate asks laws away.
normal.cn: interrogate 问问题，abrogate 把法律问走。

normal.en: Derogate subtracts a part; abrogate ends the whole.
normal.cn: derogate 削去一部，abrogate 废除全部。

normal.en: arrogate is the sound twin, but it seizes instead.
normal.cn: arrogate 是音形孪生词，但义为擅夺。

normal.en: -ation noun: abrogation appears in legal writing.
normal.cn: -ation 名词：abrogation 常见于法律文书。

abstract.en: Hear the gavel striking a law out of existence.
abstract.cn: 听法槌一击，把法律敲得灰飞烟灭。

abstract.en: See a treaty torn in two on a green table.
abstract.cn: 看一条约在绿呢桌上被撕成两半。

abstract.en: Feel the weight lift when an old rule dies.
abstract.cn: 体会旧规失效时如释重负之感。

examples.en: The court ruled that the agency could not abrogate the statute on its own.
examples.cn: 法院裁定该机构无权自行废止该法规。

examples.en: The two states agreed to abrogate their border accord peacefully.
examples.cn: 两国同意和平废除边界协定。

examples.en: Critics feared the council would abrogate long-standing traditions overnight.
examples.cn: 批评者担心委员会会一夜之间废除既有传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波罗规特」——像阿波罗神谕那样特别正式地把规矩废掉。

root: 拉丁语 abrogare：ab-（离去）+ rogare（正式提请、立法之问）。在罗马法中特指经表决废止整部法规，与 derogare（部分削减）、subrogare（以新代旧）分工。十六世纪经学术英语进入法律与神学语域，至今保持正式色彩。

sensesIntro.en: The verb moves from repealing formal instruments to ending binding customs.
sensesIntro.cn: 动词由废止正式文书延伸到终结有约束力的惯例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gavel stroke cancelling a written rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：法槌一击，成文规则当场作废。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: treaties, decrees, and statutes die by formal act.
branches.cn: 文书：条约、法令与法规经正式行为废止。

branches.en: CUSTOMS: patronage and old habits treated as implicit law.
branches.cn: 惯例：恩惠任命与旧习被视作不成文之法。

branches.en: AUTHORITY REQUIRED: only a competent body can abrogate.
branches.cn: 须有权威：唯有适格机构可行废除。

branches.en: WHOLENESS: unlike derogate, the repeal is complete.
branches.cn: 整体性：与 derogate 不同，废除是彻底的。

branches.en: FORMAL REGISTER: everyday speech prefers repeal or scrap.
branches.cn: 正式语域：日常口语更常说 repeal 或 scrap。

intro.en: Rogare, the asking-and-law-making root, seeds many formal English verbs.
intro.cn: rogare 这一「请问、立法」词根衍生出多个正式英语动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legal verbs survive in English institutional language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁法律动词保留在英语制度性语言中。

items.example: abdicate: to declare oneself away from duty

latinEntries.meaning: to repeal a statute by vote

definition_zh: 人口统计的；人口结构的；特定人群（名词义）
definition_en: relating to the structure and statistics of populations, or a group defined by shared population traits
core_image: 一张人口金字塔图，底层宽、顶层窄，每条横杠代表一个年龄组
scene: 调查表先按年龄和收入把受访者分组： The survey split respondents by demographic group before comparing answers.
sceneCN: 这里 demographic 作定语，指「按人口特征划分的」（第 3 个义项：由年龄、收入等共同特征界定的人群）；句意为调查先把受访者按人口特征分组，再比较答案。图中可辨识物件：金字塔图、年龄横杠、分组标签、统计表。

pos.zh: 人口统计的；人口结构的；人口特征的
特定人群；人口群体（如某年龄或收入层）

derivatives.zh: 人口统计数据；人群构成

senses.title: Relating to population structure
senses.definition: connected with the size, age and make-up of a population
senses.definitionCN: 与人口的规模、年龄与构成有关
senses.example: Demographic change has left more pensioners than children.
senses.exampleCN: 人口结构变化使领取养老金的人多于儿童。
senses.why: dēmos 'people' plus graphein 'write' gives the study of populations, and the adjective simply describes whatever belongs to that study.
senses.whyCN: dēmos「民众」加 graphein「书写」构成对人口的研究，形容词就描述属于这项研究的一切。

senses.title: Relating to population statistics
senses.definition: connected with the numbers collected about births, deaths, migration and age
senses.definitionCN: 与出生、死亡、迁移与年龄等收集到的数字有关
senses.example: The report opens with a demographic table by region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一张分地区的人口统计表。
senses.why: the adjective covers both the structure and the figures, so it can sit before data as easily as before change.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词同时涵盖结构与数字，因此既能修饰 change，也能修饰 data。

senses.title: A group with shared traits
senses.titleCN: 由共同特征界定的人群（名词义）
senses.definition: a section of a population defined by age, income, education or similar traits
senses.definitionCN: 按年龄、收入、教育等特征划分出来的一部分人口
senses.example: The survey split respondents by demographic group before comparing answers.
senses.exampleCN: 调查先把受访者按人口特征分组，再比较答案。
senses.why: marketers needed a countable slice of the population, so the adjective became a noun naming that slice.
senses.whyCN: 营销需要人口中可数的一块，于是形容词转为名词，命名那一块。

senses.title: The collected figures
senses.definition: the statistics themselves, usually in the plural demographics
senses.definitionCN: 指统计数字本身，通常用复数 demographics
senses.example: The demographics show a young city growing older.
senses.exampleCN: 统计数据显示，一座年轻的城市正在变老。
senses.why: once the figures are habitually referred to in the plural, demographics becomes a noun in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 当这些数字习惯上用复数指称，demographics 就独立成为名词。

senses.title: The transition model
senses.titleCN: 人口转变模型中的用法
senses.definition: belonging to the model that traces a society from high to low birth and death rates
senses.definitionCN: 属于描述社会由高出生高死亡转向低出生低死亡的模式
senses.example: Demographic transition explains the lag between falling deaths and falling births.
senses.exampleCN: 人口转变解释了死亡下降与出生下降之间的时间差。
senses.why: the model needed a fixed name, and the adjective supplied one that fits every stage of the shift.
senses.whyCN: 模式需要一个固定名称，这个形容词正好提供一个能套住各阶段的名称。

senses.title: A dividend from age structure
senses.titleCN: 人口红利：劳动年龄人口占比高带来的增益
senses.definition: the economic gain a country receives when working-age adults outnumber dependants
senses.definitionCN: 劳动年龄成年人多于受抚养者时，国家获得的经济增益
senses.example: The demographic dividend lasted two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 人口红利持续了二十年。
senses.why: economists priced the age structure, so a bulge of workers became a dividend to be spent.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家给年龄结构定了价，于是劳动力高峰成了一份可以花掉的红利。

senses.title: Ageing and shrinking
senses.definition: belonging to the trend of older populations and fewer births
senses.definitionCN: 属于人口老化、出生减少的趋势
senses.example: Demographic ageing is reshaping the labour market.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化正在重塑劳动力市场。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to any trend defined by the age profile, and ageing is now the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可接任何由年龄结构定义的走势，而老龄化如今是主要那一个。

senses.title: A market segment label
senses.definition: used by business to describe the slice of customers a product is aimed at
senses.definitionCN: 商业用来描述产品针对的那一部分顾客
senses.example: The app was built for a younger demographic.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用是为更年轻的人群打造的。
senses.why: segmentation turned the adjective into a targeting word, and the noun became shorthand for the audience itself.
senses.whyCN: 市场细分把这个形容词变成定向用词，名词则成了受众本身的简称。

intro.en: Demographic combines Greek dēmos 'the people' with -graphic from graphein 'to write'. Demography was coined in 1855 by Achille Guillard. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: demographic 把希腊 dēmos「民众」与来自 graphein「书写」的 -graphic 结合。demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dēmos meant 'the people, the common people' and also named a district; it is the root of democracy as well as demography.
items.cn: dēmos 意为「民众、平民」，也指一个行政区；它既是 demography 的词根，也是 democracy 的词根。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, to draw'; with -ia it made words for a field of writing or study, as in geography.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、刻画」；加 -ia 构成表示某一书写或研究领域的词，如 geography。

items.en: The noun demography is generally credited to Achille Guillard, who used démographie in a work of 1855.
items.cn: 名词 demography 一般归功于 Achille Guillard，他在 1855 年的一部著作中使用了 démographie。

items.en: The adjective demographic followed in the later nineteenth century, and the plural noun demographics spread in the twentieth as market research grew.
items.cn: 形容词 demographic 在 19 世纪后期出现；复数名词 demographics 随 20 世纪市场研究的发展而扩散。

items.en: The twentieth century added fixed phrases such as demographic transition and demographic dividend, turning the word into a policy instrument.
items.cn: 20 世纪又增添了 demographic transition 与 demographic dividend 等固定说法，使这个词成为政策工具。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English use of the adjective is not precisely recorded, and the exact month of Guillard's coinage is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词在英语中的最早使用没有精确记录；Guillard 造词的确切月份亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same demo- and -graphy stock that are constantly swapped; group two holds terms for describing groups of people.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 demo- 与 -graphy 词干、常被互换的词；第二组是描述人群的其他术语。

entries.definition: The discipline that studies populations; demographic is the adjective belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究人口的学科；demographic 是属于它的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural noun for population statistics or for the groups they describe, as in the demographics of a city.
entries.definitionCN: 复数名词，指人口统计数据或其所描述的群体，如一座城市的人群构成。

entries.definition: A person who studies populations; the word names a profession, not a statistic.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究人口的人；命名一种职业，而非一项统计。

entries.definition: Relating to rule by the people; it shares demo- but concerns government, not population structure.
entries.definitionCN: 与民主有关的；共享 demo-，但关乎政体而非人口结构。

entries.definition: The people counted; demographic describes their structure rather than naming them.
entries.definitionCN: 指被计数的人；demographic 描述其结构，而非命名其人。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics in general; demographic narrows this to population figures.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与统计有关；demographic 把它限定到人口数字。

entries.definition: Combining social and economic position; demographic covers age and household too.
entries.definitionCN: 结合社会与经济地位；demographic 还涵盖年龄与家庭。

entries.definition: The official counting of a population; demographic work uses it but is not identical with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指官方的人口清点；人口统计工作会使用它，但并不等同于它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: demo- 'people' + -graphic 'written': written down about the people.
normal.cn: demo-「民众」+ -graphic「书写」：关于民众的记录。

normal.en: The family runs demography, demographer, demographic, demographics, demographically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 demography、demographer、demographic、demographics、demographically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: demographic transition, demographic dividend, demographic ageing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：人口转变、人口红利、人口老龄化。

normal.en: The plural demographics usually means the figures, the singular a segment.
normal.cn: 复数 demographics 多指数据，单数多指某一人群。

normal.en: The same dēmos root appears in democracy and in epidemic's cousin epidemiology.
normal.cn: 同一 dēmos 词根也出现在 democracy 与 epidemiology 中。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid standing on a wide base and narrowing to a point.
abstract.cn: 想象一座金字塔底宽顶尖。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd sorted into coloured bands by age.
abstract.cn: 想象人群按年龄被分成不同颜色的带。

abstract.en: Picture a shop that knows exactly which age buys its bread.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店清楚哪个年龄层买它的面包。

examples.en: Demographic data show a sharp fall in the number of children.
examples.cn: 人口统计数据表明儿童数量大幅下降。

examples.en: The party's demographic base is older than it was a decade ago.
examples.cn: 该党的人口基础比十年前更老。

examples.en: Advertisers pay more for a young demographic.
examples.cn: 广告商为年轻人群付更高的价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「demo（人民）+ graphic（描绘）」——把人群按年龄收入画出来 → 人口统计的、人群的

root: 希腊 dēmos「民众、平民」+ graphein「书写」（经 -graphic）；demography 由 Achille Guillard 于 1855 年造出。英语 demographic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one view: a population is drawn as a chart, and that view is then read as structure, statistics, a targeted segment, a data set, a transition, a dividend, an ageing trend and a market label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种视角展开：把人口画成图表，这个视角再被读成结构、统计、定向人群、数据集、转变、红利、老化趋势与市场标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a population pyramid, wide at the base and narrow at the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座底宽顶尖的人口金字塔。

branches.en: THE VIEW ITSELF: what belongs to population structure and to its figures.
branches.cn: 视角本身：属于人口结构与统计数字的东西。

branches.en: A SLICE OF PEOPLE: the adjective becomes a countable segment and then a market target.
branches.cn: 人群的一小块：形容词变成可数的人群，再变成市场目标。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: demographics as a plural noun for collected figures.
branches.cn: 数字本身：demographics 作复数名词指收集到的数据。

branches.en: MODEL AND GAIN: the transition describes change, the dividend prices it.
branches.cn: 模型与增益：转变描述变化，红利为其定价。

branches.en: AGEING TREND: older populations and fewer births become a standing phrase.
branches.cn: 老化趋势：人口变老与出生减少成为固定说法。

intro.en: Demographic is built from two Greek elements; demo- is a combining form and -graphic a suffix meaning 'written or described'.
intro.cn: demographic 由两个希腊成分构成；demo- 是组合形式，-graphic 是表示「书写、描绘」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek rather than Latin: dēmos 'people' and graphein 'to write', the second also giving geography and biography.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个成分属希腊语而非拉丁语：dēmos「民众」与 graphein「书写」，后者还构成 geography 与 biography。

items.structure: Greek dēmos (people) as a combining form
items.example: Democracy and demography share this element.
items.exampleCN: democracy 与 demography 共享这一成分。

items.example: Geography writes the earth, demography writes the people.
items.exampleCN: 地理学书写大地，人口学书写人群。
人口学追踪出生与死亡。
人口学家预测了 2050 年的人口。
人口结构变化重塑劳动力。

items.example: The demographics of the town are shifting.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇的人口构成在变化。
这两座城市在人口结构上不同。

items.example: An epidemic spreads through a population.

definition_zh: 标准化的；按统一标准制作或检验的；规范化的；（贬义）千篇一律的
definition_en: made to conform to an agreed standard, or measured and judged against one
core_image: 一排原本长短不一的螺丝被同一把卡尺逐个量过，最后整齐地落进同一个量规
scene: 这里指「标准化的」。 All the parts were standardized so that any replacement would fit.
sceneCN: 这里 standardized 是「按统一标准制作的」（第 1 个义项：零件遵循同一规格而可互换）；句意：所有零件都已标准化，任何替换件都能装上。图中可辨识物件：卡尺、量规、同一规格的螺丝、装件盒。

pos.zh: 标准化的；按统一标准制作或检验的；规范化的；（贬义）千篇一律的

senses.title: Made to one agreed specification
senses.definition: made to a common size, design or specification so that one item can replace another
senses.definitionCN: 按共同的尺寸、设计或规格制作，使一件物品可以替换另一件
senses.example: Standardized containers cut the cost of loading ships.
senses.exampleCN: 标准化集装箱降低了装船成本。
senses.why: Standard first named a fixed rallying point and later an authorized model; adding -ize turns that model into a verb, and the past participle describes whatever has been made to match it.
senses.whyCN: standard 最初指固定的集结点，后指权威认定的范型；加 -ize 把这个范型变成动词，过去分词则描述已被做成与之一致的事物。

senses.title: Scored against a fixed test standard
senses.titleCN: 按固定标准评分：标准化考试
senses.definition: of a test or score, designed, administered and graded in the same way for every candidate so that results can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 指测试或分数按同一方式设计、实施与评分，使不同考生的结果可以比较
senses.example: The university accepts either the national standardized test or its own exam.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学接受全国标准化考试，也接受本校自设考试。
senses.why: Comparability is the point: if every candidate meets the same procedure and the same scoring key, the differences in score reflect differences in performance rather than differences in the test.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于可比性：如果每位考生面对同一程序与同一评分标准，分数的差异就反映表现差异，而不是测试本身的差异。

senses.title: Calibrated against a reference
senses.titleCN: 依基准标定：校准过的仪器或量值
senses.definition: of an instrument or measurement, checked against a known reference so that its readings can be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器或测量已对照已知基准进行校验，因而读数可信
senses.example: Only standardized thermometers were used in the temperature trial.
senses.exampleCN: 温度试验中只使用了经过标定的温度计。
senses.why: Metrology treats the standard as the authority; a standardized instrument is one whose readings have been tied to that authority, which is a narrower, technical version of sense one.
senses.whyCN: 计量学把标准视为权威；standardized 仪器就是读数已与该权威挂钩的仪器，这是第 1 个义项在计量领域的更窄用法。

senses.title: Brought into a common format
senses.titleCN: 统一格式：数据与记录规范化
senses.definition: of data, records or documents, converted into a common layout and set of fields so that they can be merged or compared
senses.definitionCN: 指数据、记录或文件被转换为共同的版式与字段，以便合并或比较
senses.example: The clinics standardized their forms before linking the databases.
senses.exampleCN: 各家诊所在连接数据库之前统一了表格格式。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from physical parts to information: a form that follows one standard can be read by the same machine or clerk as any other form.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻从实体零件转向信息：按同一标准制作的表格，能和其他表格一样被同一台机器或同一位职员读取。

senses.title: Following a fixed procedure
senses.definition: of a procedure or protocol, written down and followed in the same order every time so that results are reproducible
senses.definitionCN: 指程序或规程被写下来，每次按同样顺序执行，使结果可以复现
senses.example: The lab adopted a standardized procedure for storing samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室采用了标准化的样本保存程序。
senses.why: A procedure becomes a standard when it stops depending on individual habit; the participle marks the state of having been brought under that rule.
senses.whyCN: 当程序不再依赖个人习惯时，它就成为标准；过去分词标记「已被纳入该规则」的状态。

senses.title: Made uniform in spelling or usage
senses.definition: of spelling, terminology or usage, reduced to one accepted form where several variants once existed
senses.definitionCN: 指拼写、术语或用法在曾有多种变体的情况下被归并为一种被接受的形式
senses.example: Standardized spelling made the dictionary usable across regions.
senses.exampleCN: 统一的拼写让这部词典在各地区都能使用。
senses.why: Printing and schooling needed one form per word; the same authority that fixes a measure can fix a spelling, so the participle extends to language.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与学校教育需要每个词只有一种写法；能确定度量标准的权威也能确定拼写，于是过去分词扩展到语言领域。

senses.title: Made routine and interchangeable
senses.definition: of work, services or systems, organized into identical repeatable units so that people and parts can be swapped in and out
senses.definitionCN: 指工作、服务或系统被组织成相同的可重复单元，使人与零件可以随时替换
senses.example: Standardized shifts allowed nurses to move between wards.
senses.exampleCN: 标准化班次让护士可以在不同病区之间调动。
senses.why: Standardization removes local variation on purpose; what remains is a unit that fits anywhere, which is efficient and also the source of the pejorative sense that follows.
senses.whyCN: 标准化有意消除地方差异，剩下的是随处可用的单元；这带来效率，也正是随后贬义义的来源。

senses.title: Uniform to the point of blandness
senses.titleCN: 千篇一律：失去个性的统一
senses.definition: used with disapproval, describing housing, schooling or products that are so uniform that individuality and local character are lost
senses.definitionCN: 带贬义，描述住房、教育或产品过于统一，以致个性与地方特色消失
senses.example: Critics called the new district standardized and soulless.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个新城区千篇一律、没有灵魂。
senses.why: Once the word spreads from parts to people's lives, the virtue of fitting in becomes the vice of being indistinguishable, and the participle acquires this critical tone.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从零件扩展到人的生活，「适配」的优点就变成「难以区分」的缺点，过去分词由此带上批评语气。

intro.en: Standardized is an English formation: the noun standard, the verb suffix -ize and the past-participle ending -ed. Standard itself is not Latin but came through Old French, and its deeper origin is disputed.
intro.cn: standardized 是英语内部构成：名词 standard、动词词尾 -ize 与过去分词词尾 -ed。standard 本身并非源自拉丁，而是经古法语进入英语，其更深来源有争议。

items.en: Old French estandart named a rallying flag or banner, the sign around which troops gathered. English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 estandart 指集结用的旗帜或军旗，即部队聚拢所围绕的标志。英语在十三世纪借入该词。

items.en: The Old French form is generally believed to come from a Frankish compound reconstructed as *standhard, 'stand firm', from *standan 'to stand' and *hard 'hard, firm'. The starred form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 一般认为古法语形式来自法兰克语复合词，被重构为 *standhard「站稳」，由 *standan「站立」与 *hard「坚硬、牢固」构成。带星号的形式是重构，并非有记录的真实词形。

items.en: By the eighteenth century standard meant an authorized rule or model against which things are judged, a sense that developed from the fixed rallying point. The precise path and date are uncertain.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，standard 已指权威规则或范型，用来评判事物；这一义项由固定的集结点发展而来，但确切路径与年代不确定。

items.en: Standardize is an English verb of the nineteenth century, formed from standard plus -ize. It first described making weights, measures and parts conform to one model.
items.cn: standardize 是十九世纪的英语动词，由 standard 加 -ize 构成，最初描述让度量衡与零件符合同一范型。

items.en: The participle standardized spread in the twentieth century with mass production, national testing and digital records, and it took on the critical sense of 'made blandly uniform'.
items.cn: 过去分词 standardized 随大规模生产、全国性考试与数字记录在二十世纪流行，并获得「被弄得千篇一律」的批评义。

items.en: Source uncertainty (root): the deeper origin of standard is undecided, and Frankish *standhard is a reconstructed form. First-attestation uncertainty: no exact year is known for the earliest English use of standardize or standardized. No Latin source can be confirmed, so latinEntries is left empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：standard 的更深词源没有定论，法兰克语 *standhard 属重构形式。首见年代存疑：standardize 与 standardized 的英语最早书证均无确定年份。本词无法确证拉丁来源，故拉丁词条留空。

note.en: The first group separates the standard family by part of speech and level; the second gives near-synonyms for uniformity.
note.cn: 第一组按词性与层级区分 standard 词族；第二组给出表示「统一」的近义词。

entries.definition: The rule or model itself, or an adjective meaning 'normal and accepted'. Standardized describes something that has been made to match the standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或范型本身，也可作形容词表示「通常被接受的」；standardized 描述已被做成符合该标准的事物。

entries.definition: The act of bringing things to one standard; standardized is the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物统一到某一标准的动作；standardized 是由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: The process itself. Standardized is the adjective for what has undergone that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；standardized 是经历了该过程之后的形容词。

entries.definition: Falling short of the required standard. It judges quality, while standardized only says which standard was applied.
entries.definitionCN: 指低于要求的标准，评判的是质量；standardized 只说明采用了哪一标准。

entries.definition: The same in form throughout. It describes the sameness itself, not the act of imposing a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体形式相同，描述的是相同性本身，而不是施加标准的动作。

entries.definition: Behaving or appearing the same from one case to the next. It stresses reliability over a series, not conformity to a written rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个个案例之间表现一致，强调跨系列的可靠性，而非符合书面规则。

entries.definition: Adjusted to a common scale or baseline, especially in data and diplomacy. It is a technical cousin of standardized.
entries.definitionCN: 指调整到共同尺度或基线，尤其用于数据与外交；它是 standardized 的技术性近亲。

entries.definition: Able to be put in place of one another. It states the practical result of standardization, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以互相替换，说明标准化带来的实际结果，而不是动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: standard + -ize + -ed: first set the model, then make things match it.
normal.cn: standard + -ize + -ed：先立范型，再让事物与之一致。

normal.en: The family runs standard, standardize, standardization, substandard, nonstandard.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 standard、standardize、standardization、substandard、nonstandard。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: standardized test, standardized score, standardized procedure, standardized parts.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：标准化考试、标准化分数、标准化程序、标准化零件。

normal.en: A standard is a flag troops rally around; standardized parts all snap into the same slot.
normal.cn: standard 原指部队聚拢的旗帜；standardized 零件则都能卡进同一个槽位。

normal.en: The word improves parts and can belittle places: standardized bolts are good, standardized suburbs are dull.
normal.cn: 这个词既能夸零件，也能贬地方：标准化螺栓很好，标准化郊区很乏味。

abstract.en: Picture a row of screws measured by one caliper and dropped into one gauge.
abstract.cn: 想象一排螺丝被同一把卡尺量过，落进同一个量规。

abstract.en: Picture many different doors cut to one keyhole size.
abstract.cn: 想象许多不同的门都被改成同一个锁孔尺寸。

abstract.en: Picture a town where every street sign uses the same font and the same grey wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇，所有路牌用同一字体，所有墙是同一种灰色。

examples.en: Standardized shipping containers changed world trade more than any single ship design.
examples.cn: 标准化集装箱对世界贸易的改变超过任何单一船型的设计。

examples.en: The researchers used a standardized questionnaire to compare the two groups.
examples.cn: 研究人员使用标准化问卷来比较两组人群。

examples.en: Residents complained that the new housing was standardized and had lost all local character.
examples.cn: 居民抱怨新住房千篇一律，失去了所有地方特色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「standard（标准）+ ized」——被同一把尺子量过一遍 → standardized 标准化的

root: 英语 standard（源出古法语 estandart「军旗、集结点」，一般认为来自法兰克语重构形式 *standhard「站稳」）+ -ize + -ed；非拉丁来源，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from physical parts to testing, instruments, data, procedures, spelling, work routines and finally to the critical sense of a life made too uniform.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实体零件依次扩展到考试、仪器、数据、程序、拼写、工作班次，最后落到「生活被弄得过于统一」的批评义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many uneven pieces are measured against one gauge until they match.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多不齐的零件被同一个量规量到彼此一致。

branches.en: PHYSICAL CONFORMITY: parts and instruments are matched or calibrated to one reference.
branches.cn: 物理一致：零件与仪器被做成或校准到同一基准。

branches.en: FAIR COMPARISON: one test procedure lets different candidates be ranked on the same scale.
branches.cn: 公平比较：同一考试程序让不同考生在同一尺度上排序。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL ROUTINE: forms and protocols follow one layout and one order.
branches.cn: 制度常规：表格与规程遵循同一版式、同一顺序。

branches.en: ONE ACCEPTED FORM: spelling and terminology are reduced to a single variant.
branches.cn: 唯一被接受的形式：拼写与术语被归并为一种变体。

branches.en: SWAPPABLE UNITS AND THEIR COST: work becomes interchangeable, and places lose character.
branches.cn: 可互换单元及其代价：工作变得可互换，地方则失去特色。

intro.en: Standardized is standard plus the verb suffix -ize plus the past-participle ending -ed, which here works as an adjective ending meaning 'having been made so'.
intro.cn: standardized 由 standard 加动词词尾 -ize、再加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成；此处 -ed 作形容词词尾，意为「已被做成那样」。

latinIntro.en: Standard has no confirmed Latin source: it came through Old French from a Frankish form reconstructed as *standhard. Because the Latin line cannot be confirmed, no latinEntries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: standard 没有可确证的拉丁来源：它经古法语来自被重构为 *standhard 的法兰克语形式。由于无法确证拉丁来源，本词条不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: made to conform to a standard
items.meaningCN: 已被做成符合某一标准的
items.example: The clinic uses standardized intake forms.
items.exampleCN: 该诊所使用标准化的接诊表格。

items.meaning: to bring things to one standard
items.meaningCN: 使事物统一到某一标准
items.example: The alliance agreed to standardize radio frequencies.
items.exampleCN: 联盟同意统一无线电频率。

items.example: Standardization of the bolts lowered repair costs.
items.exampleCN: 螺栓的标准化降低了维修成本。

items.example: The agency sets the standard for drinking water.
items.exampleCN: 该机构制定饮用水标准。
不合格的电线引发了火灾。

items.example: Nonstandard dialects are still fully grammatical.
items.exampleCN: 非标准方言同样完全合乎语法。

items.meaning: a person or body that standardizes
items.meaningCN: 推行标准化的人或机构
items.example: The standardizer must consult the workers who use the tools.
items.exampleCN: 标准化推行者必须咨询实际使用工具的人。

items.meaning: one who carries the flag, or a leading representative

definition_zh: v. 随便翻看，浏览；（动物）吃嫩叶；n. 浏览
definition_en: to look through a book, shop or website without a fixed purpose; of animals, to feed on leaves and shoots
core_image: 地铁上有人随手翻着杂志，一页也没读进去
scene: 她在地铁上随手翻着杂志，一篇也没读进去。 On the train she browsed a magazine without reading a single article.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：browse 指随意翻看浏览；句意是她在地铁上随手翻杂志，一篇也没读进去。

浏览

senses.title: To look through casually
senses.definition: to look at books, goods or pages without a fixed aim
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定目的地翻看书、商品或网页
senses.example: He browsed the shelves for twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他在货架间逛了二十分钟。
senses.why: The word first described animals feeding on shoots.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描述动物吃嫩芽。

senses.title: Of animals, to feed on leaves
senses.definition: to eat leaves, twigs or shoots, as deer and goats do
senses.definitionCN: 像鹿和山羊那样吃叶子、细枝或嫩芽
senses.example: Deer browsed at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿在林边啃食嫩叶。
senses.why: Browsing is slow, scattered eating, which suits a slow look.
senses.whyCN: 「浏览」是慢而零散的进食，正合慢而零散地看。

senses.title: To move through web pages
senses.definition: to move from page to page on the internet
senses.definitionCN: 在互联网上从一页到另一页地看
senses.example: She browsed the site for a cheap flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她浏览网站找便宜机票。
senses.why: Digital browsing repeats the same unhurried, unfixed movement.
senses.whyCN: 数字浏览重复了同样从容、无固定目标的移动。

intro.cn: browse 最初意为吃嫩芽与枝条，可能来自法语 brost。

items.en: Brost means a young shoot or bud.
items.cn: brost 意为嫩芽。

items.cn: browse 意为啃食嫩枝。

entries.definition: To read quickly for the main points.

entries.definition: To look over quickly for specific information.

entries.definition: To turn pages quickly.

entries.definition: To move casually from site to site.

normal.en: People browse on shelves.

normal.en: A browser browses web pages.

abstract.en: A shop entered with no list.

abstract.en: Pages turning faster than reading.

examples.en: Deer browse the young trees at dusk.
