definition_zh: 半岛；半岛状地带；伸入水中的陆块
definition_en: a piece of land almost surrounded by water but still joined to the mainland
core_image: 一块三面被水包围、只有一条窄颈连着大陆的陆地
scene: 一座灯塔立在半岛的尽头。 A lighthouse stands at the tip of the peninsula.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「三面环水、一面连陆的陆地」（第 1 个义项：伸入水中的陆块）；句意为灯塔立在半岛尖端。

pos.zh: 半岛；半岛状地带

senses.title: Land almost surrounded by water
senses.titleCN: 半岛：三面环水、一面连陆的陆地
senses.definition: a piece of land that projects into water and is joined to the mainland by a narrow neck
senses.definitionCN: 伸入水中、以狭窄地颈与大陆相连的陆块
senses.example: A lighthouse stands at the tip of the peninsula.
senses.exampleCN: 一座灯塔立在半岛的尽头。
senses.why: Latin paene 'almost' plus insula 'island' names land that is almost an island, which is exactly the shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「几乎」加「岛」构成「几乎是岛」，正是这种地形的形状。

senses.title: A peninsula-shaped area
senses.definition: any land area shaped like a peninsula, even if small
senses.definitionCN: 任何形状像半岛的陆地区域，即使很小
senses.example: The garden ends in a small peninsula of grass.
senses.exampleCN: 花园尽头是一小块半岛状的草地。
senses.why: The shape, not the size, defines the word, so small projections can take it too.
senses.whyCN: 决定这个词的是形状而非大小，因此小的突出地块也能用它。

senses.title: A geographic unit for study
senses.definition: a peninsula treated as a unit of physical geography
senses.definitionCN: 作为自然地理单元看待的半岛
senses.example: The peninsula has its own rainfall pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这个半岛有自己的一套降水规律。
senses.why: Geographers treat the joined landmass as one unit because its water on three sides shapes its climate.
senses.whyCN: 地理学者把这块连陆的陆地当作一个单元，因为三面环水塑造了它的气候。

senses.title: The settled region on a peninsula
senses.definition: the towns and countryside on a peninsula, seen as a region
senses.definitionCN: 半岛上的城镇与乡村，作为一片地区看待
senses.example: Fishing villages ring the peninsula.
senses.exampleCN: 渔村环绕着这个半岛。
senses.why: The landform becomes a human region once people settle it, so the word can name the place rather than the shape.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有人定居，地形就变成人文区域，因此这个词可以指地方而非形状。

senses.title: A strategic salient
senses.definition: a military position that projects into enemy ground on three sides
senses.definitionCN: 三面伸入敌方阵地的军事位置
senses.example: The troops held the peninsula against attacks from three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 部队守住了这个三面受敌的突出部。
senses.why: A salient and a peninsula share the same exposed shape, so military language borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 突出部与半岛共享同一种暴露的形状，军事语言便借用了这个词。

senses.title: A projection into another area
senses.definition: a part of something that projects into a different area
senses.definitionCN: 某物伸入另一区域的部分
senses.example: A dry peninsula of sand reached into the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 一段干燥的沙质突出部伸进沼泽。
senses.why: Any narrow projection can be pictured as a peninsula, which is how the metaphor works.
senses.whyCN: 任何狭长的突出部分都能被想象成半岛，比喻就是这样运作的。

senses.title: The neck joining it to the mainland
senses.titleCN: 半岛与大陆相连的地颈
senses.definition: the narrow link by which a peninsula is attached to the mainland
senses.definitionCN: 半岛连接大陆的狭窄地带
senses.example: A road crosses the peninsula's narrow neck.
senses.exampleCN: 一条路穿过半岛狭窄的地颈。
senses.why: Without the neck the land would be an island, so the joining strip is central to the definition.
senses.whyCN: 没有地颈，这块陆地就是岛，因此连接地带是定义的核心。

senses.title: A named cultural region
senses.definition: a peninsula used in a proper name for a cultural or political region
senses.definitionCN: 用于文化或政治区域专名的半岛
senses.example: The Korean peninsula has a long shared history.
senses.exampleCN: 朝鲜半岛有悠久的共同历史。
senses.why: Proper names such as the Iberian Peninsula turn the landform into a political and cultural label.
senses.whyCN: 伊比利亚半岛之类的专名把地形变成政治与文化标签。

intro.en: Peninsula comes from Latin paeninsula, literally 'almost an island', built on paene 'almost' and insula 'island'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁语，字面义为「几乎是岛」，由表示「几乎」与「岛」的两个词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: paene meant 'almost, nearly', and it marks how close the land comes to being an island.
items.cn: 拉丁语词意为「几乎、将近」，标出这块陆地离岛有多近。

items.en: insula 'island' also gives English insular, isolate and insulation through related forms.
items.cn: 拉丁语「岛」还通过相关形式给出英语中表示岛屿的、使孤立的与绝缘的词。

items.en: paeninsula joined the two words for land that is nearly but not fully surrounded by water.
items.cn: 两个词合成后，指几乎但并未完全被水包围的陆地。

items.en: English took the word directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, keeping the geographic sense.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入，保留了地理义。

items.en: Later use extended the shape to military salients, small projections and proper names of regions.
items.cn: 后来的用法把这种形状扩展到军事突出部、小型突出地块与地区专名。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed, and dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：英语最早书证没有确切记录，年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to peninsula; group two holds other coastal landforms that are easily mixed up with it.
note.cn: 第一组是字形或读音接近该词的词；第二组是容易与它混淆的其他海岸地形词。

entries.definition: Relating to a peninsula; it is the adjective while peninsula is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指与半岛有关的；它是形容词，而本词是名词。

entries.definition: Relating to an island, or narrow in outlook; it comes from Latin insula, the second half of peninsula.
entries.definitionCN: 指岛屿的，或心胸狭隘的；来自拉丁语「岛」，正是本词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Material that stops heat or sound; it looks similar but belongs to a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻隔热量或声音的材料；形似但属于另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The condition of being a peninsula or of having an isolated outlook; it is a rare derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 指处于半岛状态或具有孤立心态；属罕见派生词。

entries.definition: A high point of land projecting into the sea; it is a point, not a nearly enclosed mass.
entries.definitionCN: 指伸入海中的高地角；它是一个尖端，不是几乎被围住的陆块。

entries.definition: A narrow piece of land projecting into the sea, usually with a cliff; smaller and narrower than a peninsula.
entries.definitionCN: 指伸入海中的狭长陆地，通常带悬崖；比半岛更小更窄。

entries.definition: A long narrow bank of sand or shingle projecting into water; it is built by currents, not by the mainland shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指伸入水中的狭长沙洲或砾石洲；由水流堆积而成，不是大陆形状。

entries.definition: Land completely surrounded by water; the key contrast is that a peninsula still touches the mainland.
entries.definitionCN: 指四面完全被水包围的陆地；关键差别是半岛仍与大陆相连。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paene 'almost' + insula 'island': almost an island, still joined to land.
normal.cn: 「几乎」加「岛」：几乎是岛，却仍连着陆地。

normal.en: The family runs peninsula, peninsular, peninsularity and the ecological peninsula effect.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词、其形容词、其状态名词，以及生态学的半岛效应。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: the Iberian Peninsula, a narrow peninsula, the tip of the peninsula.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：伊比利亚半岛、狭长半岛、半岛尖端。

normal.en: The key test is the neck: with a link to the mainland it is a peninsula, without one it is an island.
normal.cn: 关键看地颈：与大陆相连就是半岛，没有连接就是岛。

normal.en: The same shape serves as a metaphor for a military salient or any narrow projection.
normal.cn: 同一形状可比喻军事突出部或任何狭长突出部分。

abstract.en: Picture a hand with three fingers in water and the wrist still on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手三根手指浸在水里，手腕仍搭在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that almost leaves the main topic but stays tied to it by one thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话几乎离开主题，却被一根线牵住。

abstract.en: Picture a stage that juts into the audience while still joined to the back wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个伸进观众席、却仍连着后墙的舞台。

examples.en: The peninsula shelters the harbour from the open sea.
examples.cn: 这个半岛为港口挡住了外海。

examples.en: They walked the length of the peninsula in a single afternoon.
examples.cn: 他们用一个下午走完了整个半岛。

examples.en: The narrow neck of the peninsula floods at high tide.
examples.cn: 半岛狭窄的地颈在涨潮时会被淹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「怕你死啦」：三面都是水，只剩一条窄路回家——半岛。

root: 拉丁语 paene（几乎）+ insula（岛）构成 paeninsula「几乎是岛」，指三面环水、一面连陆的陆地。英语 peninsula。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: land nearly cut off by water. The shape is then applied to small projections, a geographic unit, a settled region, a military salient, any narrow projection, the joining neck and a named cultural region.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：几乎被水切断的陆地。这个形状随后用于小型突出地块、地理单元、居住区域、军事突出部、任何狭长突出部分、连接地颈以及专名中的文化区域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broad hand of land reaching into water, held to the mainland by a narrow wrist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只伸进水中的宽大陆掌，被狭窄的手腕连在大陆上。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the projecting mass and the neck that keeps it from being an island.
branches.cn: 形状：突出的陆块与使它不至于成为岛的地颈。

branches.en: SMALL PROJECTIONS: the same outline works at the scale of a garden or a sandbank.
branches.cn: 小型突出：同一轮廓可用于花园或沙洲的尺度。

branches.en: GEOGRAPHY: three sides of water make the peninsula one climatic unit.
branches.cn: 地理：三面环水使半岛成为一个气候单元。

branches.en: HUMAN LABEL: settlements and proper names turn the shape into a place.
branches.cn: 人文标签：定居点与专名把形状变成地方。

branches.en: SALIENT: military language borrows the exposed outline.
branches.cn: 突出部：军事语言借用了这种暴露的轮廓。

intro.en: Peninsula is a Latin compound of an adverb and a noun, and both parts also build other English words.
intro.cn: 该词是副词与名词构成的拉丁复合词，两部分还构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin paene 'almost' and insula 'island' combine in paeninsula; insula also gives insular and isolate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「几乎」与「岛」合成该词；「岛」还给出表示岛屿的形容词与使孤立的动词。

items.example: The prefix of meaning says the land is nearly an island.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示「几乎」的成分说明这块陆地差不多是岛。

items.example: The noun half supplies the island image.
items.exampleCN: 名词那一半提供岛的意象。

items.example: A lighthouse stands at the tip of the peninsula.

items.exampleCN: 半岛的道路沿着海岸走。
半岛状态塑造了这个地区的贸易。

items.example: Insular habits kept the village closed.
items.exampleCN: 岛屿式的习惯让村子封闭。
洪水能把半岛与外界隔开。

items.example: The peninsula effect predicts fewer species at the tip.
items.exampleCN: 半岛效应预测越靠尖端物种越少。

definition_zh: 天然卫星；自然形成、绕行星运行的天体（与人造卫星相对）
definition_en: a naturally formed body that orbits a planet or a smaller solar-system body
core_image: 讲解牌前，一颗灰白小球绕着大球转，旁边的小牌写明它未经任何发射
scene: 展厅的讲解牌上，一颗灰白小球绕着一颗大球运行，旁边注明它并非任何人造装置。 The label explains that a natural satellite formed without any human launch.
sceneCN: 这里 natural satellite 指「自然形成、绕行星运行的天体」（第 1 个义项：与人造卫星相对）；句意为牌子说明天然卫星未经任何人类发射而形成。图中可辨识物件：讲解牌、灰白小球、大球、绕行箭头、展台灯。

pos.zh: 天然卫星（可数，复数指多颗）

collocations.zh: 天然卫星与人造卫星之别

senses.title: A moon, not a machine
senses.titleCN: 天然形成的卫星，而非机器
senses.definition: a body that formed by natural processes and orbits a planet or smaller body
senses.definitionCN: 由自然过程形成、绕行星或更小天体运行的天体
senses.example: The label explains that a natural satellite formed without any human launch.
senses.exampleCN: 牌子说明天然卫星未经任何人类发射而形成。
senses.why: the phrase exists mainly to draw a line: after 1957 'satellite' could mean a machine, so 'natural' had to be added.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语主要用来划界：1957 年后 satellite 可指机器，因此必须加上 natural。

senses.title: The moons of the solar system
senses.titleCN: 太阳系各行星的卫星群
senses.definition: collectively, the hundreds of moons counted around the planets and dwarf planets
senses.definitionCN: 合计指各行星与矮行星周围数以百计的卫星
senses.example: The solar system's natural satellites number in the hundreds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系的天然卫星数以百计。
senses.why: once telescopes and probes found moons everywhere, the phrase became the collective label for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 当望远镜与探测器在各处发现卫星后，这个短语成了它们的集合标签。

senses.title: Tidal locking
senses.definition: the state in which a natural satellite keeps one face toward its planet
senses.definitionCN: 天然卫星始终以同一面朝向其行星的状态
senses.example: Most large natural satellites are tidally locked to their planets.
senses.exampleCN: 多数大型天然卫星都被潮汐锁定在各自的行星上。
senses.why: close moons are slowed by their planet's tides until spin and orbit match, a fact the phrase often carries.
senses.whyCN: 近距卫星被行星潮汐拖慢，直到自转与公转同步，这个短语常承载这一事实。

senses.title: How they form
senses.definition: used of the processes that produce moons: accretion in a disk, impact debris or gravitational capture
senses.definitionCN: 指产生卫星的过程：盘中吸积、撞击碎片或引力俘获
senses.example: Capture is one route by which a natural satellite joins a planet.
senses.exampleCN: 俘获是天然卫星加入某行星的一条途径。
senses.why: formation is the main way astronomers classify moons, so the phrase often appears beside models of origin.
senses.whyCN: 形成方式是天文学家给卫星分类的主要依据，因此这个短语常与起源模型同现。

senses.title: Regular and irregular moons
senses.titleCN: 规则卫星与不规则卫星
senses.definition: used in the classification by orbit: regular moons go the planet's way in near-circular paths, irregular ones do not
senses.definitionCN: 按轨道分类：规则卫星顺行星自转方向近圆运行，不规则卫星则不然
senses.example: The planet's irregular natural satellites travel far out and backwards.
senses.exampleCN: 该行星的不规则天然卫星在远处逆行。
senses.why: orbit shape records origin, so the phrase pairs naturally with the regular and irregular labels.
senses.whyCN: 轨道形状记录着起源，因此这个短语自然与规则、不规则两类标签搭配。

senses.title: Worlds with oceans and volcanoes
senses.titleCN: 有海洋与火山的卫星世界
senses.definition: used of large moons studied as worlds in their own right, with ice, atmospheres or volcanism
senses.definitionCN: 指被当作独立世界研究的大型卫星，有冰、大气或火山活动
senses.example: One natural satellite of Jupiter may hold a deep ocean under its ice.
senses.exampleCN: 木星的一颗天然卫星可能在冰下拥有深海。
senses.why: the phrase marks that these bodies are not mere points but places with geology worth studying.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标明这些天体不只是光点，而是有值得研究的地质的地方。

senses.title: Naming rules
senses.definition: used in the context of the official naming of moons by the international astronomical body
senses.definitionCN: 用于国际天文机构对卫星的正式命名语境
senses.example: A newly found natural satellite waits years for an official name.
senses.exampleCN: 新发现的天然卫星要等上数年才获正式名字。
senses.why: because such bodies are numerous and faint, an official register is needed, and the phrase appears in those rules.
senses.whyCN: 这类天体数量多且暗淡，需要一份正式名录，而这个短语就出现在这些规则里。

senses.title: Watching one from earth
senses.definition: used of amateur or telescopic observation of a moon's brightness, phase or motion
senses.definitionCN: 指业余或望远镜观测卫星的亮度、相位与运动
senses.example: A small telescope can follow the natural satellite's nightly motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一台小望远镜就能追踪这颗天然卫星每夜的运动。
senses.why: before spacecraft, everything known about moons came from watching their motion, so the phrase belongs to observation as well as to theory.
senses.whyCN: 在航天器之前，关于卫星的一切都来自观测其运动，因此这个短语既属理论也属观测。

intro.en: Natural satellite joins natural, from Latin natura 'nature', to satellite, from Latin satelles 'attendant'. The phrase became standard when artificial satellites made the distinction necessary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: natural satellite 由 natural（源自拉丁 natura「本性」）与 satellite（源自拉丁 satelles「随从」）组合。当人造卫星使区分成为必要，这个短语才成为标准。年代均为约数。

items.en: Natura meant birth, character and the order of things, from nasci 'to be born'; naturalis 'of nature' came from it.
items.cn: natura 意为出生、本性、万物秩序，来自 nasci「出生」；naturalis「自然的」由此而来。

items.en: Satelles meant an attendant or guard; its deeper origin is uncertain and possibly not Latin.
items.cn: satelles 意为随从或护卫；其更深来源不确定，可能并非拉丁语固有。

items.en: From the seventeenth century satellite named a moon, and natural was added when precision was needed.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起 satellite 指卫星，需要精确时会加上 natural。

items.en: Artificial satellites made the contrast unavoidable, and 'natural satellite' became the standard technical phrase.
items.cn: 人造卫星使这一对照不可避免，natural satellite 成为标准技术短语。

items.en: Modern planetary science uses the phrase for every moon, from lumpy small bodies to Titan-sized worlds.
items.cn: 现代行星科学用这个短语指所有卫星，从形状不规则的小天体到土卫六大小的世界。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated, and the etymology of satelles remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早用例没有可靠年代；satelles 的词源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the terms that differ only by origin; group two holds words for a small companion body.
note.cn: 第一组是只因来源不同而区分的术语；第二组是表示小伴体的词。

entries.definition: The general word for anything orbiting a larger body, natural or built.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指绕更大天体运行之物，天然的或人造的。

entries.definition: A human-made craft in orbit; it is defined by contrast with the natural kind.
entries.definitionCN: 在轨的人造航天器；其定义正与天然一类相对。

entries.definition: The common word for a natural satellite, especially the earth's; it is shorter and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 天然卫星的日常词，尤指地球的；更短、更不技术化。

entries.definition: The body a moon orbits; the two words mark the two ends of one relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 卫星所绕的天体；两词标记同一关系的两端。

entries.definition: A very small moon, often a temporary ring particle; the -let suffix marks small size.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的卫星，常为暂时的环中颗粒；-let 后缀标记小。

entries.definition: A neutral term for a smaller body travelling with a larger one, used when the class is unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 指随较大天体运行之较小天体的中性说法，用于类别不明时。

entries.definition: A body that orbits the primary in a pair; it says nothing about how it formed.
entries.definitionCN: 双天体系统中绕主天体运行者；不涉及形成方式。

entries.definition: Broken pieces in orbit, natural or artificial; it is not a coherent satellite.
entries.definitionCN: 在轨的碎块，天然或人造；并非成形的卫星。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实搭配、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: natural 'formed by nature' + satellite 'attendant': a moon that formed on its own.
normal.cn: natural「自然形成的」+ satellite「随从」：自行形成的卫星。

normal.en: The phrase became standard after 1957 to separate moons from machines.
normal.cn: 1957 年后这个短语成为标准，用来把月球与机器分开。

normal.en: Most large moons are tidally locked, showing one face to their planet.
normal.cn: 多数大型卫星被潮汐锁定，只以一面朝向行星。

normal.en: Regular moons follow the planet's spin; irregular ones are captured and often retrograde.
normal.cn: 规则卫星顺着行星自转；不规则卫星多为被俘获且常逆行。

normal.en: The family runs satellite, moon, moonlet, artificial satellite, lunar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 satellite、moon、moonlet、artificial satellite、lunar。

abstract.en: Picture a pebble that has been going round a boulder since before any map existed.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石子，在有地图之前就绕着巨石转。

abstract.en: Picture a dancer always facing the same partner, never showing her back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个舞者始终面向同一搭档，从不转身。

abstract.en: Picture a child born in a house and never once leaving the yard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个生在这屋里、从未离开院子的孩子。

examples.en: Earth's natural satellite is unusually large for its planet.
examples.cn: 地球的天然卫星相对其行星大得异常。

examples.en: New natural satellites are still being found around Saturn.
examples.cn: 土星周围仍在发现新的天然卫星。

examples.en: A natural satellite can be captured from a passing asteroid.
examples.cn: 天然卫星可能由路过的小行星被俘获而成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自然的（natural）＋ 撒特莱特（satellite）」——自己长出来、绕着转的伴星 → 天然卫星

root: natural 源自拉丁 natura「本性」（nasci「出生」）+ -alis；satellite 源自拉丁 satelles「随从」，更深来源不确定；短语在 1957 年后与人造卫星对举而固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses define the term by contrast with machines, then apply it to the solar system's moons, to locking, formation, orbit classes, living worlds, naming and observation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先用与人造物的对照定义术语，再用于太阳系卫星群、潮汐锁定、形成方式、轨道类别、有活动世界的卫星、命名规范与观测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey ball circling a larger one, with no launch tower anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗灰球绕着更大的球，周围没有任何发射塔。

branches.en: THE CENSUS: the phrase counts every moon that qualifies.
branches.cn: 清点：这个短语清点所有合格的卫星。

branches.en: PHYSICS OF ARRIVAL: locking and formation explain how a moon settles into place.
branches.cn: 到来的物理：锁定与形成解释了卫星如何安顿下来。

branches.en: CLASSES AND WORLDS: orbit shape sorts them, and some become places in their own right.
branches.cn: 类别与世界：轨道形状给它们分类，有些则成为独立的地方。

branches.en: NAMING AND SEEING: official registers and small telescopes both handle these faint bodies.
branches.cn: 命名与看见：正式名录与小望远镜都在对付这些暗淡天体。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: 'natural' is the whole point of the phrase.
branches.cn: 对照：「natural」正是这个短语的全部要点。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-derived words: an adjective from natura and a noun from satelles, with no prefix involved.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源的词构成：一个来自 natura 的形容词，一个来自 satelles 的名词，不涉及前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin natura and naturalis supply the first word, satelles the second; the compound phrase itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 natura 与 naturalis 提供第一个词，satelles 提供第二个；短语本身是近代英语。

items.example: The root also gives natural and native.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 natural 与 native。

items.example: A natural arch spans the cove.
items.exampleCN: 一座天然拱桥横跨小湾。

items.example: The satellite is faint but regular.
items.exampleCN: 这颗卫星暗淡但有规律。

items.example: The label names a natural satellite.
items.exampleCN: 牌子上写的是一颗天然卫星。

items.example: Artificial satellites outnumber the visible moons.
items.exampleCN: 人造卫星数量超过可见卫星。

items.example: A moonlet may survive only a few years.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小卫星可能只存在几年。

definition_zh: adj. 意气相投的，合得来的；宜人的，适宜的
definition_en: pleasant because of a shared nature or a good fit
core_image: 两个人一开口就发现想法彼此合拍
scene: 他发现和她相处格外投缘，一聊就是一下午。 He found her congenial company and they talked all afternoon.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：congenial 指意气相投的；句意是他觉得与她相处很投缘。

pos.zh: 意气相投的；宜人的

senses.title: Easy to be with
senses.definition: pleasant because you share tastes with someone
senses.definitionCN: 因趣味相投而令人愉快
senses.example: He found her congenial company.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得与她相处很投缘。
senses.why: Latin genius meant a shared inborn nature.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 genius 指共有的天性。

senses.title: Suited to a place or task
senses.definition: pleasant and suitable for a place or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某地或某活动合适而舒适
senses.example: The climate is congenial to health.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的气候有益健康。
senses.why: The fit is between a person and a setting.
senses.whyCN: 这种契合发生在人与环境之间。

intro.en: Congenial joins con-, together, to genius, an inborn nature.
intro.cn: congenial 由 con-（共同）与 genius（天性）构成。

items.en: Genius meant a guardian spirit or inborn nature.
items.cn: genius 指守护神或天性。

items.en: Genialis meant of birth or festive.
items.cn: genialis 意为天生的或节庆的。

items.en: Congenial described minds of one kind.
items.cn: 十七世纪 congenial 形容同类的心性。

items.en: It spread to pleasant rooms and climates.
items.cn: 十八世纪扩展到宜人的房间与气候。

items.en: It came to mean simply agreeable.
items.cn: 十九世纪引申为「合意」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gen root; the near-meaning group names pleasant fits.
note.cn: 形近组共享词根 gen；近义组列出令人愉快的契合。

entries.definition: Friendly and cheerful.
entries.definitionCN: 亲切愉快的。

entries.definition: Present from birth.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来的。

entries.definition: Exceptional natural ability.
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的天赋。

entries.definition: Enjoyable and easy to accept.
entries.definitionCN: 愉快而易于接受的。

entries.definition: Warm toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 待人和善的。

entries.definition: Able to exist together well.
entries.definitionCN: 能和谐共处的。

entries.definition: Enjoyable to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的。

normalIntro.en: Congenial people share a nature and fit together easily.
normalIntro.cn: congenial 的人天性相近，容易合拍。

normal.en: Genius meant inborn nature.
normal.cn: genius 曾指天性。

normal.en: Con- means together.
normal.cn: con- 意为共同。

normal.en: Congenial means of the same nature.
normal.cn: congenial 意为天性相同。

normal.en: A congenial room suits the people in it.
normal.cn: 宜人的房间与人相称。

normal.en: Genial is warm; congenial is a good fit.
normal.cn: genial 是热络，congenial 是契合。

abstract.en: Two keys turning the same lock.
abstract.cn: 两把转动同一把锁的钥匙。

abstract.en: A chair shaped to the sitter.
abstract.cn: 按坐者身形做的椅子。

abstract.en: A tune that meets its harmony.
abstract.cn: 遇上和声的旋律。

examples.en: The two of them were congenial from the start.
examples.cn: 他们俩一开始就很投缘。

examples.en: She enjoys congenial company at dinner.
examples.cn: 她喜欢晚餐时有投缘的伙伴。

examples.en: The soil is congenial to these plants.
examples.cn: 这土壤适合这些植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（共同）+ gen（天性）+ -ial（…的）→ 天性相合，即投缘的。

root: 拉丁 con（共同）+ genius（天性）→ congenialis（同性的）→ 英语 congenial

sensesIntro.en: A good fit between people, or between a person and a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 人与人之间，或人与环境之间的良好契合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people finding their thoughts in step
core.cn: 核心意象：两人发现想法步调一致

branches.en: A talk that runs for hours.
branches.cn: 一聊就是几小时的谈话。

branches.en: A host who puts guests at ease.
branches.cn: 让客人自在的主人。

branches.en: A room that suits its use.
branches.cn: 适合其用途的房间。

branches.en: A climate kind to the body.
branches.cn: 对身心友善的气候。

branches.en: A fit that feels effortless.
branches.cn: 毫不费力的契合。

intro.en: Congenial belongs to the gen family of birth and nature.
intro.cn: congenial 属表「出生、天性」的 gen 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin genius is inborn nature and genialis means of birth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genius 指天性，genialis 意为天生的。

definition_zh: 功能；功能性；功能特性
definition_en: the set of things a system or device can actually do, or the quality of working as intended
core_image: 一台机器的控制面板上，每个按钮按下后都有对应的灯亮起
scene: 这里指「功能」。 Reviewers praised the app's functionality but asked for a simpler menu.
sceneCN: 这里 functionality 是「功能、功能特性」（第 1 个义项：系统实际能做哪些事）；句意：评审称赞这款应用的功能，但要求菜单更简洁。图中可辨识物件：手机界面、功能按钮、设置菜单、勾选清单。

pos.zh: 功能；功能性；功能特性

senses.title: The set of things it can do
senses.titleCN: 功能集合：它到底能做哪些事
senses.definition: the total set of operations that a product or system is able to perform
senses.definitionCN: 产品或系统能够执行的全部操作
senses.example: The update added functionality for offline editing.
senses.exampleCN: 这次更新增加了离线编辑功能。
senses.why: functio means 'performance'. Functionality lists the performances a thing can give, taken together as one property.
senses.whyCN: functio 意为“执行、履行”。functionality 把一件东西能给出的各种“执行”合在一起，当作一个属性。

senses.title: Working order
senses.titleCN: 功能性：还能不能正常用
senses.definition: the state of working correctly and being usable for its intended purpose
senses.definitionCN: 正常运作、能按其用途使用的状态
senses.example: The repair restored full functionality to the pump.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修让水泵恢复了完整功能。
senses.why: Here the word is a condition, not a list. Something has functionality when its parts still perform their functions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是一种状态，而不是清单。当零件仍能履行各自功能时，该物就具有 functionality。

senses.title: Software features
senses.titleCN: 软件功能：版本里带了什么
senses.definition: the features offered by a piece of software, considered as a selling point
senses.definitionCN: 某软件提供的功能特性，被视为卖点
senses.example: Users compare the functionality of the two apps before choosing one.
senses.exampleCN: 用户会先比较两款应用的功能，再作选择。
senses.why: Software made the word common. A program is judged by what its buttons actually do, which is a list of performances.
senses.whyCN: 软件让这个词流行。程序按按钮实际能做什么来评判，而那是一张“执行清单”。

senses.title: Bodily function
senses.titleCN: 生物机能：器官还在工作
senses.definition: in biology or medicine, the normal operation of an organ or system
senses.definitionCN: 生物学或医学中器官或系统的正常运作
senses.example: The treatment preserved kidney functionality in most patients.
senses.exampleCN: 该治疗在多数患者身上保住了肾功能。
senses.why: Biological functionality keeps the original sense of functio: an organ has a job, and functionality is whether it still does it.
senses.whyCN: 生物机能保留 functio 的本义：器官有一项职责，functionality 就是它是否仍在履行。

senses.title: Extra features
senses.titleCN: 附加功能：有当然好，没有也能用
senses.definition: additional capabilities beyond the essential ones, often optional
senses.definitionCN: 超出基本必需之外的附加能力，常为可选
senses.example: The basic model lacks the connectivity functionality of the larger one.
senses.exampleCN: 基础型号缺少大型号的联网功能。
senses.why: This sense is comparative: functionality can be counted and added. More features mean more functions, though not always more usefulness.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是比较性的：功能可以被计数、被添加。功能多意味着“执行”多，但未必更有用。

senses.title: Testing that it works
senses.definition: the aspect of quality assurance concerned with whether each feature works as specified
senses.definitionCN: 质量保证中关注每项功能是否按规格运作的方面
senses.example: Functionality testing found two buttons that did nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 功能测试发现两个按钮按了没反应。
senses.why: Testing splits a product into functions and checks each. The word shifts from the property to the activity of verifying it.
senses.whyCN: 测试把产品拆成功能逐项检查。这个词从属性转到验证属性的活动。

senses.title: How useful it really is
senses.titleCN: 实用程度：功能多不等于好用
senses.definition: the practical usefulness of a product, as distinct from the number of features listed
senses.definitionCN: 产品的实际有用程度，区别于所列功能的数量
senses.example: The camera's functionality is limited by its slow autofocus.
senses.exampleCN: 这款相机的实用性受限于它缓慢的自动对焦。
senses.why: A long feature list can hide weak performance. Functionality in this sense asks whether the functions actually serve the user.
senses.whyCN: 长长的功能清单可能掩盖薄弱性能。这个义项的 functionality 问的是这些功能是否真的服务于用户。

senses.title: Completeness of function
senses.titleCN: 功能完整性：该有的都有
senses.definition: the degree to which all expected functions are present and working
senses.definitionCN: 所有预期功能都存在并正常运作的程度
senses.example: The prototype has the functionality of the final product but not its finish.
senses.exampleCN: 样机具备最终产品的功能，但没有它的外观工艺。
senses.why: This sense measures completeness against a specification. The question is not how many features but whether any required one is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项对照规格衡量完整性。问题不是功能多少，而是有没有漏掉必需的那一项。

intro.en: Functionality is functional plus -ity. Functional comes from function, from Latin functio 'performance', from fungi 'to perform'. The root is fung-, not fund-, and has nothing to do with 'bottom'.
intro.cn: functionality 是 functional 加 -ity。functional 来自 function，而 function 出自拉丁 functio“执行”，源头是 fungi“履行”。词根是 fung-，不是 fund-，与“底部”无关。

items.en: fungi meant 'to perform, discharge, carry out'. The past participle functus gives the whole family; the root is unrelated to fundus 'bottom'.
items.cn: fungi 意为“履行、执行、完成”。过去分词 functus 生出整个词族；这个词根与 fundus“底部”无关。

items.en: functio named a performance or discharge, including a duty or an official role. The word already carried the idea of a job being done.
items.cn: functio 命名一次执行或履行，包括职责与公职。这个词已带有“完成一项任务”的观念。

items.en: English function arrives in the 16th century with both the 'duty, role' sense and the mathematical sense. The mathematical use grows in the 17th and 18th centuries.
items.cn: 英语 function 于 16 世纪进入，兼有“职责、角色”义与数学义。数学用法在 17 至 18 世纪发展。

items.en: Functional adds -al to function, meaning 'relating to function'. In the 19th and 20th centuries it also means 'practical rather than decorative', especially in design.
items.cn: functional 在 function 后加 -al，意为“与功能有关的”。19 至 20 世纪它也指“实用而非装饰的”，尤见于设计。

items.en: Functionality adds -ity to functional, forming the abstract noun. The word becomes common with 20th-century engineering and computing.
items.cn: functionality 在 functional 后加 -ity，构成抽象名词。这个词随 20 世纪工程与计算机而流行。

items.en: In the late 20th century software marketing fixes functionality as a countable feature set, giving the plural functionalities wide use.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期软件营销把 functionality 固定为可计数的功能集，使复数 functionalities 广泛使用。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the funct- stem; the near-meaning group all concern what a thing can do or how well it does it.
note.cn: 形近组共享 funct- 词干；近义组都关于某物能做什么或做得多好。

entries.definition: a purpose, role or mathematical relation. It is one function; functionality is the whole set or the working state.
entries.definitionCN: 用途、职责或数学关系。它是单个功能；functionality 是整套功能或运作状态。

entries.definition: relating to function, or practical. It describes a thing; functionality names the property.
entries.definitionCN: 功能的；实用的。它描述事物；functionality 命名属性。

entries.definition: a failure to work properly. mal- means 'badly', so it is the negative of function, while functionality can still be partial.
entries.definitionCN: 故障；运作失常。mal- 意为“坏地”，是 function 的反面，而 functionality 仍可能是部分的。

entries.tag: what it is able to do
entries.definition: the power or ability to do something. It is broader and can include potential not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的能力。它更宽泛，可包含尚未使用的潜力。

entries.definition: a distinctive part or function of a product. It is one item; functionality is the collection.
entries.definitionCN: 产品的特色部分或功能。它是一项；functionality 是集合。

entries.definition: the quality of being useful, or a public service. It stresses benefit rather than operation.
entries.definitionCN: 有用性，或公用事业。它强调益处，而非运作。

entries.definition: how well a machine or system carries out its tasks. It adds speed and reliability to the bare idea of function.
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统执行任务的优劣。它在“功能”之上加了速度与可靠性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fungi 'perform' gives function: functionality is the sum of what a thing can perform.
normal.cn: fungi“履行”生出 function：functionality 就是一件东西能履行的全部事情。

normal.en: function, functional, functionality form the noun-adjective-noun chain of one root.
normal.cn: function、functional、functionality 构成同一词根的名词—形容词—名词链条。

normal.en: core functionality and full functionality are the two common extremes: the minimum and the complete set.
normal.cn: core functionality 与 full functionality 是两个常见极端：最低必需与完整集合。

normal.en: Keep fund- and fung- apart: foundation is 'bottom', function is 'perform'.
normal.cn: 把 fund- 与 fung- 分开：foundation 是“底部”，function 是“执行”。

normal.en: A feature is one thing it does; functionality is the whole list or the fact that it still works.
normal.cn: feature 是它做的一件事；functionality 是整张清单，或它仍能工作的状态。

abstract.en: Think of a control panel where every button lights up a different lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一块控制面板，每个按钮都点亮一盏不同的灯。

abstract.en: Think of a toolbox: the tools are features, and the box's usefulness is its functionality.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工具箱：每件工具是功能点，整个箱子的用处就是它的 functionality。

abstract.en: Think of a body whose organs each do their job, so the whole person still works.
abstract.cn: 想象身体各器官各司其职，整个人因此仍能运作。

examples.en: The new version adds functionality without changing the interface.
examples.cn: 新版本增加了功能，却没有改动界面。

examples.en: Restoring functionality after the flood took four months.
examples.cn: 洪水后恢复功能花了四个月。

examples.en: Functionality testing is separate from usability testing.
examples.cn: 功能测试与易用性测试是分开的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “方（fun）壳（ction）里能做的事”——一个方壳子机器，按下按钮能干什么 → functionality 功能

root: 拉丁 fungi“履行、执行” → functio“执行” → 英语 function → functional → functionality；注意词根是 fung-，与 fund-（底部）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one question, asked of a machine, a program or an organ: what can it actually perform, and does it still perform it?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个问题，用来问机器、程序或器官：它实际能执行什么，现在还能不能执行？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a control panel where each button lights its own lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块控制面板，每个按钮点亮自己的灯。

branches.en: THE SET: the full list and the optional extras are the same collection seen with and without its edges.
branches.cn: 集合：完整清单与附加功能，是同一集合带着边界和不带边界的样子。

branches.en: WORKING ORDER: full functionality and functional completeness both ask whether anything required has stopped.
branches.cn: 运作状态：完整功能与功能完整性，都在问是否有必需功能停了。

branches.en: SOFTWARE: features become selling points, turning performances into a comparison table.
branches.cn: 软件：功能变成卖点，把“执行”变成一张对比表。

branches.en: BODY: an organ keeps its job, and functionality is whether it still discharges it.
branches.cn: 身体：器官有其职责，functionality 就是它是否仍在履行。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: testing each feature and judging real usefulness both ask whether the list means anything in practice.
branches.cn: 判断：逐项测试与评判实际用处，都在问这张清单在现实中是否有意义。

intro.en: Functionality is functional plus -ity. The funct- stem means 'perform', -ion makes an action noun, -al makes a relational adjective and -ity makes the quality noun.
intro.cn: functionality 是 functional 加 -ity。funct- 词干意为“履行”，-ion 构成动作名词，-al 构成关系形容词，-ity 构成性质名词。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from fungi 'perform' through functio 'performance' to English function. Relatives include functional, malfunction, defunct and functionary.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 fungi“履行”经 functio“执行”到英语 function。同族词包括 functional、malfunction、defunct、functionary。

items.meaning: a role, purpose or mathematical relation
items.meaningCN: 功能；职责；函数（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The heart's function is to pump blood.

items.meaningCN: 功能的；实用的（-al 关系形容词）
items.example: The chair is functional rather than beautiful.
items.exampleCN: 这把椅子重在实用，不在美观。

items.meaning: the set or quality of functions
items.meaningCN: 功能；功能性（-ity 性质名词）

items.example: The two parts are functionally identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个部件在功能上完全相同。

items.example: A sensor malfunction stopped the line.
items.exampleCN: 一个传感器故障让生产线停了。
这种药治疗肝功能障碍。

items.meaningCN: 已废止的；不再运作的（de-“离开”+ functus“已履行”）
items.exampleCN: 那家停产的工厂被卖掉了。

items.meaning: an official with a defined role
items.meaningCN: 官员；职员（-ary 人称名词）
items.example: A junior functionary signed the form.
items.exampleCN: 一名低级职员签了那张表。

definition_zh: 使卑下；使谦卑；降低自己的身份
definition_en: to make someone or yourself seem lower in rank, status, or dignity
core_image: 一个人被按下头去，头顶的高度被一寸寸压低
scene: 颁奖礼上，昔日的主帅要在众人面前向新王行礼。 The defeated general was forced to abase himself before the new king.
sceneCN: 这里 abase 是「使卑下、使谦卑」（第 2 个义项：主动降低自己的身份）；句意为战败的将军被迫在新王面前自贬行礼。

pos.zh: 使卑下；使降低身份
（常与反身代词连用）自贬；谦卑自己

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「屈辱；自贬；降位」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被贬低的；屈辱的」
同根近义词，加 de- 构成，义为「贬低；贬值」

senses.title: To lower someone else's dignity
senses.definition: to lower the rank, honour, or dignity of another person, often by force or humiliation
senses.definitionCN: 压低另一个人的地位、荣誉或尊严，常通过强制或羞辱
senses.example: The tyrant abased his rivals in front of the whole court.
senses.exampleCN: 暴君在全朝廷面前羞辱贬抑他的对手。
senses.why: The low base of a building holds everything up; to abase is to push a person down to that low level.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物的 base 是最低的基座；abase 就是把人压到那个最低的高度。

senses.title: To lower oneself
senses.definition: to behave so as to lower one's own dignity or status, usually to show humility or to beg
senses.definitionCN: 以压低自己身份或地位的方式行事，通常为表示谦卑或乞求
senses.example: He abased himself and begged for the queen's forgiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 他自贬身份，乞求王后的宽恕。
senses.why: When no one else pushes, the person bends down alone; the reflexive use keeps the same downward motion with oneself as the object.
senses.whyCN: 没有别人施压时，人自己弯下身去；反身用法保持同一个向下的动作，只是对象换成了自己。

senses.title: To reduce the value or standing of a thing
senses.titleCN: 贬低事物的价值或地位
senses.definition: to lower the worth, quality, or standing of something abstract, such as a title or a currency
senses.definitionCN: 降低某抽象事物（如头衔、货币）的价值、品质或地位
senses.example: The endless scandals abased the office of mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 接连不断的丑闻贬损了市长这一职位。
senses.why: What works on persons extends to things; anything with standing or worth can be pressed down to a lower level.
senses.whyCN: 作用于人的动作延伸到事物上；凡有地位或价值者都可被压到更低的水准。

intro.en: Abase comes straight from the Old French abaisser, to lower, which was built on a Late Latin verb meaning to make low.
intro.cn: abase 直接来自古法语 abaisser「使降低」，后者建立在晚期拉丁语「使变低」的动词之上。

items.en: Bassiare meant to lower, formed on bassus, meaning low or short.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bassiare 意为使降低，由 bassus「低的；矮的」构成。

items.en: Abaisser kept the same meaning: to bring down, to lower.
items.cn: 古法语 abaisser 保留了同一含义：使下降、使降低。

items.en: The verb spread with courtly and religious usage, describing bowing and humility.
items.cn: 中古法语动词随宫廷与宗教用语传播，描写鞠躬与谦卑。

items.en: English borrowed abase in the sixteenth century, first for lowering pride and rank.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 abase，最早用于压低骄傲与地位。

items.en: Today it survives mainly in the reflexive phrase abase oneself.
items.cn: 如今该词主要存于反身短语 abase oneself 之中。

note.en: Abase shares its French family with abash, and its Latin base with abject.
note.cn: abase 与 abash 同属法语词族，又与 abject 共享拉丁语 base 词根。

entries.definition: to make someone embarrassed, not humble
entries.definitionCN: 使人窘迫，而非使人谦卑；词尾 -ash 与 -ase 拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: the noun form of abase, meaning humiliation or lowering
entries.definitionCN: abase 的名词形式，义为屈辱、自贬

entries.definition: to lower the quality or value of something
entries.definitionCN: 降低某物的品质或价值；同用拉丁语 base 一族，但前缀不同

entries.definition: to make someone feel less important
entries.definitionCN: 使人感到不重要；语气较温和，可指正当的谦卑

entries.definition: to make someone feel very ashamed
entries.definitionCN: 使人深感羞耻；强调羞辱的情绪冲击

entries.definition: to lower someone's dignity or standing
entries.definitionCN: 降低某人的尊严或地位；与 abase 意义最接近

normalIntro.en: The base inside the word gives five anchors for memory.
normalIntro.cn: 词中的 base（基座）给记忆提供五个抓手。

normal.en: a- + base: push someone down to the base level.
normal.cn: a-（去）＋ base（基座）：把人压到基座的高度。

normal.en: abasement is the noun: the state of being pushed low.
normal.cn: abasement 是名词：被压低的状态，即屈辱。

normal.en: debase lowers value; abase lowers dignity.
normal.cn: debase 贬低价值；abase 贬低尊严。

normal.en: abase oneself: you bend down by yourself.
normal.cn: abase oneself：自己弯下身去，自贬。

normal.en: Compare abash: shame in the face, not rank.
normal.cn: 对比 abash：那是脸红的窘迫，不是身份的贬低。

abstract.en: Picture an elevator that only goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象一部只能下行的电梯。

abstract.en: See a proud peacock pushed to a stone base.
abstract.cn: 看见一只骄傲的孔雀被按到石质基座上。

abstract.en: Feel the floor drop one rank lower.
abstract.cn: 感到脚下的地板又往下沉了一个等级。

examples.en: He abased himself to win back the king's favour.
examples.cn: 他自贬身份以赢回国王的宠爱。

examples.en: The cruel remarks were meant to abase her before her colleagues.
examples.cn: 那些刻薄的话意在使她在同事面前受辱。

examples.en: Such conduct abases the honour of the whole family.
examples.cn: 这种行为贬损了整个家族的名誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅卑视」——鹅被压得低下头，显出一副卑微的样子

root: 古法语 abaisser「使降低」＝ a-（源自拉丁 ad-）＋ baisser「使变低」，baisser 来自晚期拉丁语 bassiare，词根 bassus「低的」。与英语 base「基座」同源。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move one downward motion: from pushing another down, to bending oneself, to cheapening a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用同一个向下的动作：从压低别人，到自己弯腰，再到贬低事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person pushed down until the head is level with the base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被压下去，头与基座齐平。

branches.en: PUSHING DOWN ANOTHER: rank and honour are lowered by force.
branches.cn: 压低他人：地位与荣誉被强力压低。

branches.en: BENDING ONESELF: the same motion done alone as humility or begging.
branches.cn: 自己弯腰：同样的动作独自完成，出于谦卑或乞求。

branches.en: PRESSING A THING DOWN: worth and standing of abstract things sink.
branches.cn: 压低事物：抽象事物的价值与地位下沉。

branches.en: OUTSIDE FORCE: someone or something does the pressing.
branches.cn: 外力作用：由他者施压。

branches.en: ONE DOWNWARD LINE: every sense is a fall toward the base.
branches.cn: 同一条下行线：每个义项都是向基座的坠落。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, with one Latin root and one French prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态：一个拉丁词根加一个法语前缀。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin bassiare is recorded, and bassus is attested, so the root is historical.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bassiare 有文献记录，bassus 亦见于记载，词根有史可查。

items.example: It turns the verb into an action.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变为一个动作。

items.example: It is the direct source of abase.
items.exampleCN: 它是 abase 的直接来源。

items.example: It underlies the Old French verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是古法语动词的基础。

items.example: It is the shared root of base.
items.exampleCN: 它是 base 的共同词根。

items.example: It keeps the Latin root in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中保留了拉丁词根。

items.example: It forms debase, to lower value.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 debase，指贬低价值。

items.example: Its opposite shows what abase removes.
items.exampleCN: 它的反义显示了 abase 所去除的东西。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「屈辱；自贬」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被贬低的」

definition_zh: 抽象；抽象概念；抽象艺术；心不在焉
definition_en: the act of taking a general idea out of concrete things, such an idea itself, abstract art, or a state of being lost in thought
core_image: 从一堆具体事例里抬起眼睛，只握住共同的那一点
scene: 讨论会上，大家还在争论具体案例，主持人却在白板上写下一条适用于所有案例的规律。 The debate moved from cases to a level of abstraction.
sceneCN: 这里 abstraction 是「抽象化、抽象层次」（第 1 个义项：从具体事物中抽出共同观念的过程）；句意为讨论从具体案例转向抽象层面。

pos.zh: 抽象；抽象概念；抽象艺术；心不在焉

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形式，义为「抽象的」，也可作动词「提取」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「抽象地」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，义为「心不在焉的」

senses.title: The act of drawing out a general idea
senses.definition: the process of separating a general quality or idea from particular examples
senses.definitionCN: 把共同的性质或观念从具体实例中分离出来的过程
senses.example: Good teaching moves slowly from examples to abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教学从例子慢慢走向抽象。
senses.why: The suffix -tion names an action, so abstraction first means the mental act of pulling a common feature out of many cases.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -tion 表示动作，因此 abstraction 首先指从众多案例中抽出共同特征的心智活动。

senses.title: A general idea so obtained
senses.definition: a general concept considered apart from the things that show it
senses.definitionCN: 脱离体现它的具体事物而被考虑的一般概念
senses.example: Truth and beauty are abstractions until a person meets them.
senses.exampleCN: 在有人亲身遇见之前，真与美都只是抽象概念。
senses.why: Once the act is finished, the result stands on its own, so the noun shifts from the process to the idea produced.
senses.whyCN: 动作完成后结果独立存在，于是名词从过程转向所产生的观念。

senses.title: Abstract art
senses.definition: art that represent forms and colours rather than recognizable objects
senses.definitionCN: 表现形式与色彩、而非可辨认物象的艺术
senses.example: The museum devoted a whole wing to geometric abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把整整一翼用于几何抽象艺术。
senses.why: Painting that removes the object until only shape remains repeats the same withdrawal, so the style takes the noun too.
senses.whyCN: 绘画把物体移除到只剩形状，重复了同一种抽离，于是这种风格也使用该名词。

senses.title: Absent-mindedness
senses.definition: a state of being so deep in thought that one ignores surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 沉思到忽略周围环境的状态
senses.example: He stared at the kettle, lost in abstraction.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着水壶，完全出了神。
senses.why: A mind drawn away from the present scene repeats the literal Latin image, and the word came to name that mental absence.
senses.whyCN: 心智从当前场景被抽走，重复了拉丁语字面意象，这个词便用来指那种心神不在的状态。

intro.en: Abstraction adds the Latin action ending to the same stem as abstract, so its history follows the verb's.
intro.cn: abstraction 在 abstract 的同一词干上加了拉丁语动作后缀，其历史跟随那个动词。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull' and supplied the root of the family.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，提供了这个词族的词根。

items.en: The verb abstrahere meant 'to draw away'.
items.cn: 动词 abstrahere 意为「抽走」。

items.en: abstractio named the act of drawing away, formed with the -tio ending.
items.cn: abstractio 指抽走的动作，由 -tio 后缀构成。

items.en: Old French abstraction carried the learned noun into medieval use.
items.cn: 古法语 abstraction 把这个学术名词带入中世纪用法。

items.en: English abstraction first meant a quality considered apart from its subject.
items.cn: 英语 abstraction 最初指脱离主体而被考虑的性质。

items.en: Modern usage adds abstract art and the everyday phrase lost in abstraction.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了抽象艺术，以及日常短语「出神」。

note.en: The first group gathers forms of the same Latin family; the second gathers words for generality, summary, and daydreaming.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁词族的各种形式；第二组收表示概括、摘要与走神的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and verb from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词与动词形式，名词即由它构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning deep in thought and unaware of surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的、出神的」。

entries.definition: A pulling toward, from the same Latin trahere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸引」，同出拉丁语 trahere。

entries.definition: A broad statement drawn from particular cases.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「概括」，由具体案例得出的一般陈述。

entries.definition: A general idea formed in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「概念」，在头脑中形成的一般观念。

entries.definition: An organized set of ideas explaining something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理论」，解释事物的系统观念。

entries.definition: A pleasant train of thought while awake and distracted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「白日梦」，清醒却分神时的愉快思绪。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -tion pattern and the art sense; the abstract hooks picture a mind stepping up from cases to a rule.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 -tion 构词规律与艺术义；抽象记忆点想象心智从案例走上一条规律。

normal.en: Abstraction is the -tion noun of abstract, so it names the act or the result.
normal.cn: abstraction 是 abstract 的 -tion 名词，指动作或结果。

normal.en: A level of abstraction is the standard phrase in academic writing.
normal.cn: a level of abstraction 是学术写作中的标准短语。

normal.en: Geometric abstraction names art built from pure shapes.
normal.cn: geometric abstraction 指由纯形状构成的艺术。

normal.en: Lost in abstraction describes someone staring away from the room.
normal.cn: lost in abstraction 形容一个人盯着远处、不在现场。

normal.en: Abstract art and the abstract idea share one history of removal.
normal.cn: 抽象艺术与抽象观念共享同一段「抽离」的历史。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting one clean line out of a crowded drawing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从拥挤的图画里提起一根干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture a whiteboard rule written after the examples are erased.
abstract.cn: 想象例子被擦掉后白板上留下的一条规律。

abstract.en: Picture a man at a kettle, eyes fixed on nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人守着水壶，眼神落在空处。

examples.en: The course teaches abstraction step by step from real data.
examples.cn: 这门课从真实数据出发，一步步教抽象。

examples.en: Equality is an abstraction that laws must make concrete.
examples.cn: 平等是个抽象概念，必须由法律使之具体。

examples.en: Her abstraction in meetings often hides a sharp mind.
examples.cn: 她在会上出神，往往掩着一个敏锐的头脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯特拉克申」——把具体案例擦掉，白板上剩下的那条规律就叫抽象。

root: 拉丁语 abstrahere（抽走）的-action 名词 abstractio；核心义是「抽出共同点的动作及其结果」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the act of drawing out, to the idea obtained, to art that drops the object, to a mind drawn away from the room.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从抽出的动作，走到得到的观念，再到丢掉物体的艺术，最后是心神离开现场的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind stepping up from cases to one shared rule
core.cn: 核心意象：心智从具体案例登上一级共同的规律

branches.en: The mental act of separating a shared feature.
branches.cn: 分离出共同特征的心智动作。

branches.en: The general idea that remains after the act.
branches.cn: 动作之后留下的一般观念。

branches.en: Art that keeps form and drops the recognizable object.
branches.cn: 保留形式、丢掉可辨认物体的艺术。

branches.en: A mind pulled away from the present scene.
branches.cn: 被抽离当下场景的心神。

branches.en: The process and its product share one noun.
branches.cn: 过程与产物共用同一个名词。

intro.en: The noun is built from the same Latin pulling stem, with the action ending -tion and a family of adjective and adverb forms.
intro.cn: 这个名词由同一拉丁「拉」词干加动作后缀 -tion 构成，并带一串形容词与副词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin abstractio is the direct ancestor, formed from abstrahere with the action suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abstractio 是直接祖先，由 abstrahere 加动作后缀构成。
